target.title: fix(acp): preserve legacy replay state during doctor repair
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users upgrading from the retired file-backed ACP replay ledger could have migration run during ACP gateway startup instead of the explicit Doctor repair flow. A failed or interrupted import could leave ambiguous replay state or stale legacy files.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ACP runtime now opens only the canonical shared SQLite ledger. `openclaw doctor --fix` exclusively owns the legacy import: it atomically claims the source, validates every session and event, reconciles crash retries, repairs derived byte accounting, commits transactionally, and retains malformed or conflicting state for inspection. No SQLite schema, config, CLI, or protocol surface changes.

## User Impact

ACP startup no longer reads or mutates `acp/event-ledger.json`. Operators with legacy replay state can migrate it through Doctor without silent partial imports or deletion of newer replacement state. Normal users see no behavior change.

target.title: fix(browser): honor abortSignal during Playwright click-and-hold delay
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`clickViaPlaywright`'s click-and-hold delay in `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` slept with a bare `setTimeout(resolve, delayMs)`, where `delayMs` can be up to `ACT_MAX_CLICK_DELAY_MS = 5_000` (`act-policy.ts:22`). The interaction `AbortSignal` is already in scope and is checked via `throwIfInteractionAborted(signal)` right before and after the sleep — but the sleep itself was not abortable.

When the signal fires mid-hold, the caller-visible promise does reject promptly (the `abortPromise` race in `awaitActionWithAbort`, `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts:488`), but the *action chain* is orphaned: the ref'd 5 s timer keeps sleeping after the caller is gone, then throws at the post-delay check. While orphaned it pins the event loop for the remainder of the hold, and it delays the navigation-guard teardown that only runs after the action settles — the delayed-navigation observation plus the 250 ms grace and the final `assertPageNavigationCompletedSafely` (`pw-tools-core.interactions.ts:569-590`), and with an SSRF policy active the `page.route("**")` interception installed by `withPageNavigationRequestGuard` (`pw-session.ts:1663`) stays attached to the tab for the rest of the hold as well.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hold is now `await sleepWithAbort(delayMs, signal)` (`packages/retry/src/index.ts:21`, re-exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env`, already imported elsewhere in this plugin, e.g. `sleep` in `cdp.helpers.ts`). `sleepWithAbort` clears its timer and rejects on abort, so the orphaned chain unwinds at the abort event instead of after the full remaining delay. The pre/post `throwIfInteractionAborted(signal)` checks are unchanged, so behavior with no signal or no abort is identical.

The surfaced error is unchanged: `clickViaPlaywright` registers its abort listener (which rejects the race with `signal.reason`) before the action starts, so the race still rejects with the original abort reason — the proof below shows byte-identical rejection messages before and after. No new config, no new env, no SDK surface change.

Pattern reference: #108561 (merged) did the same `setTimeout` → `sleepWithAbort` swap for the Discord gateway READY backoff. Sibling #109617 covers the browser tab-discovery poll; this PR covers the click-and-hold hold delay — disjoint code paths.

## User Impact

- Cancelling an agent browser click with a hold delay (e.g. a 5 s click-and-hold) no longer leaves an orphaned action chain sleeping in the background: the timer is cleared at the abort event and the event loop can drain ~immediately (proof: 5010 ms → 338 ms).
- The post-interaction navigation guard (delayed-navigation observation, grace window, final safety recheck, and request interception when an SSRF policy is configured) is released at the abort instead of up to 5 s later, so follow-up interactions on the same tab no longer run under a stale, aborted interaction's guard state.
- Happy path is untouched: without an abort the click still waits the full `delayMs` before dispatching (locked by regression test).

## Evidence

### Signal path — full chain (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool opts | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 708 | `const signal = opts.signal` |
| Abort race | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 713-740 | `abortPromise` rejects with `signal.reason`; listener registered before the action runs |
| Hold delay (this PR) | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 758 | `await sleepWithAbort(delayMs, signal)` — timer cleared + rejection on abort |
| Sleep impl | `packages/retry/src/index.ts` | 21 | `sleepWithAbort`: `clearTimeout` + `reject(new Error("aborted", { cause: signal.reason }))` on the abort event |
| Race | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 488-506 | `Promise.race([actionPromise, abortPromise])`; late action rejection swallowed to avoid unhandled rejections |
| Guard teardown | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 569-590 | grace + `assertPageNavigationCompletedSafely` run in `finally` once the action settles — now reached at abort time |

### Real behavior proof — production `clickViaPlaywright`, real `AbortController`, wall-clock

Uncommitted proof script drives the production `clickViaPlaywright` (`resolvedPage` stub whose `locator()` returns an observed locator, `selector` + `delayMs: 5000`, no CDP connection), aborts 100 ms into the 5 000 ms hold, then measures `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` Timeout entries and the `beforeExit` timestamp (when the event loop could actually drain). No mocks, no vitest.

**Before fix (main @ 9638c3ae07)**

```json
{
  "delayMs": 5000,
  "abortAtMs": 100,
  "events": [["hover", 2], ["abort()", 106], ["settled", 149]],
  "callerRejected": true,
  "rejectionMessage": "proof: user cancelled click-and-hold",
  "rejectElapsedMs": 149,
  "hoverFired": true,
  "clickFired": false,
  "timeoutResourcesAfterReject": 1,
  "eventLoopDrainedAtMs": 5010,
  "verdict": "BUG: caller rejected but the orphaned hold-delay timer pins the event loop for the full 5000ms"
}
```

**After fix (this PR)**

```json
{
  "delayMs": 5000,
  "abortAtMs": 100,
  "events": [["hover", 4], ["abort()", 106], ["settled", 138]],
  "callerRejected": true,
  "rejectionMessage": "proof: user cancelled click-and-hold",
  "rejectElapsedMs": 138,
  "hoverFired": true,
  "clickFired": false,
  "timeoutResourcesAfterReject": 0,
  "eventLoopDrainedAtMs": 338,
  "verdict": "FIXED: abort clears the hold-delay timer; event loop drains right after the abort"
}
```

Every field is independently checkable: `timeoutResourcesAfterReject` counts `"Timeout"` entries in `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` after the caller already rejected (1 = the orphaned 5 000 ms sleep; 0 = cleared by the abort), and `eventLoopDrainedAtMs` is the `process.beforeExit` timestamp relative to t0. The rejection message is byte-identical before/after — the abort-reason error surface is unchanged.

### Control-red (mutation) verification

The new regression test fails on the unpatched code and passes on this branch:

| Version | `unwinds the hold-delay action chain promptly when aborted mid-delay` | `still waits the full hold delay before clicking when not aborted` |
|---|---|---|
| main @ 9638c3ae07 | **fails** — post-abort navigation recheck still pending 1 000 ms after the abort (orphan sleeps the full 5 000 ms first) | passes |
| this PR | **passes** — recheck completes within the 250 ms observation + 250 ms grace after the abort | passes |

Revert is exactly the production hunk above (`sleepWithAbort(delayMs, signal)` → bare `setTimeout(resolve, delayMs)`); no test edits between runs.

### Regression test

`extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.click-delay.abort.test.ts` (colocated, uses the shared `pw-tools-core.test-harness.ts` mocks): aborts a real `AbortController` 100 ms into a 5 000 ms hold and asserts (a) rejection with the original abort reason, (b) `locator.click` never fires, (c) the existing force-disconnect-on-abort call still happens with `reason: "click aborted"`, and (d) the orphaned chain's navigation recheck settles promptly instead of after the full hold. Second test locks the happy path: without abort, the click fires only after the full 5 000 ms.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.click-delay.abort.test.ts \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.navigation-guard.test.ts \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.evaluate.abort.test.ts \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.batch.test.ts \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.set-input-files.test.ts

 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  60 passed (60)
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.ts \
    extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.click-delay.abort.test.ts
(exit 0, no findings)
```

### tsgo

```
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json
(exit 0, 0 errors)
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users attaching PNG images from the Android or Apple chat and iOS share surfaces would have them changed to JPEG before the gateway received them. That changed the filename and MIME type and discarded PNG transparency.

PNG attachments from OpenClaw native clients now reach the gateway as image/png with a .png filename and preserved alpha. Large PNGs are downscaled to the existing transport budget instead of silently changing format. JPEG, HEIC, WebP, and GIF behavior is unchanged.

target.title: fix: gateway.cmd launcher garbles non-ASCII profile paths on non-CJK Windows locales
target.body:
Closes #108774

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows users whose profile path contains non-ASCII characters outside the CJK range (Turkish, Cyrillic, Greek, Western European accents, ...) can install OpenClaw but the managed Gateway never starts: the generated `gateway.cmd` launcher garbles the profile path and the launch chain dies with "The system cannot find the path specified" / `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

#107751 fixed this failure for CJK locales by encoding the launcher in the system ANSI code page — but only on locales where ANSI == OEM, and it deliberately left windows-125x hosts on plain UTF-8 ("ANSI bytes would just be a different flavor of wrong there"). On those hosts (e.g. Turkish: ANSI 1254, OEM 857) cmd.exe still reads the UTF-8 launcher in its OEM code page and the mojibake from #108774 persists.

## Why This Change Was Made

cmd.exe parses batch files with the **console code page**, which a fresh console (Task Scheduler, Startup folder, double-click) initializes from the boot-time registry `OEMCP` — not from the ANSI page, and not from whatever a parent session last `chcp`'d to. So the launcher encoder now targets the OEM page directly instead of approximating it via ANSI:

- `resolveWindowsOemEncoding()` (new, `src/infra/windows-encoding.ts`) reads `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Nls\CodePage\OEMCP` once (cached) through a narrow `queryWindowsRegistryValue` export that reuses the existing reg.exe query logic in `src/infra/windows-install-roots.ts`.
- `encodeWindowsLauncherScript` (`src/infra/windows-launcher-encoding.ts`) encodes non-ASCII `.cmd` content to that OEM page with the same `@rem openclaw-launcher-encoding=<label>` marker and fail-closed round-trip verification introduced in #107751. The `CMD_ANSI_EQUALS_OEM_ENCODINGS` special case is deleted: on CJK locales OEMCP == ACP, so those hosts resolve the identical labels (gbk/big5/shift_jis/euc-kr/windows-874) and produce byte-identical launchers — no behavior change there.
- Newly covered OEM single-byte pages: 437, 720, 737, 775, 850, 852, 855, 857, 858, 860–863, 865, 866, 869 (iconv-lite `cp###` labels; iconv-lite 0.7.2 is already a root dependency since #107751).
- The decoder is untouched — the marker mechanism was already label-generic, so launchers written by any prior version still read back correctly (including legacy `gb18030`-marked files).

Design notes:

- **Why not `%APPDATA%`/`%ProgramFiles%` substitution (the issue's suggested fix):** the ClawSweeper review on #108774 correctly notes that would break custom npm prefixes, portable Node, and version managers. This fix keeps the installer-resolved paths and makes the encoding correct instead.
- **Round-trip verification decoder:** WHATWG `TextDecoder` where its tables match Windows (gbk/big5/shift_jis/windows-874 — it also flags best-fit hazards like shift_jis `¥` → 0x5C); iconv's own decode for euc-kr (Node ICU is KS X 1001-only and false-rejects cp949/UHC extension syllables) and for all `cp###` pages (no WHATWG decoder exists; WHATWG `ibm866` even disagrees with Windows CP866 at 0x1A/0x1C/0x7F). Safe because iconv-lite never best-fits — unmappable characters become `?` and fail the round-trip, aborting the install with the existing clear error.
- **Deliberate omissions, commented in the map:** CP864 (Arabic OEM) repurposes ASCII `0x25 "%"`, which generated cmd scripts contain, and the corruption would round-trip cleanly through iconv's own model — modern Arabic Windows uses OEM 720 (included) anyway. CP1258 (Vietnamese, the one locale whose OEMCP is a windows-125x page) is omitted because iconv-lite cannot round-trip Vietnamese combining forms; it keeps today's UTF-8 fallback instead of turning mojibake into a hard install error. Hosts with the "UTF-8 worldwide" beta (OEMCP 65001) keep plain UTF-8, which is correct there.

## User Impact

`openclaw gateway install` + `gateway start` now works for Windows accounts with Turkish/Cyrillic/Greek/Western-European/etc. non-ASCII usernames — previously the P0 release-blocker path in #108774. CJK users see byte-identical output to #107751. ASCII-only installs are untouched (encoder still short-circuits before any code-page probe).

## Evidence

**Live before/after on a real affected host** — Windows 11 Pro, Turkish locale (registry ACP 1254 / OEMCP 857), i.e. exactly the ANSI≠OEM case #107751 left open. A launcher with `buildTaskScript`-shaped content (`cd /d`, `set "OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=..."`, node invocation) pointing into a `...\ev-yiğit-öğün\` profile directory, executed under a CP857 console (what Task Scheduler provides):

Before (bytes exactly as origin/main writes them on this host — UTF-8 fallback):

```
Sistem belirtilen yolu bulamıyor.            <- cd /d failed ("The system cannot find the path specified")
Error: Cannot find module 'C:\...\ev-yi─şit-├Â─ş├╝n\probe.js'   <- UTF-8 bytes misread as CP857
exit code: 1
```

After (bytes from the fixed `encodeWindowsLauncherScript()`, real production function + real registry read, which resolved `cp857` and emitted the `@rem openclaw-launcher-encoding=cp857` marker):

```
PROBE_OK cwd=C:\...\scratchpad\ev-yiğit-öğün
PROBE_OK stateDir=C:\...\scratchpad\ev-yiğit-öğün\state
exit code: 0
```

**Tests** (all pass, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ...`): `src/infra/windows-launcher-encoding.test.ts`, `src/infra/windows-encoding.test.ts`, `src/daemon/schtasks.test.ts`, `src/daemon/schtasks.install.test.ts`, `src/infra/windows-task-restart.test.ts` — 49 tests. New regression cases: cp857 Turkish path round-trip with marker, cp850 Western European, OEMCP-65001 stays UTF-8, unrepresentable characters on a single-byte OEM page fail the install fail-closed. All #107751 CJK cases (GBK/UTF-8 byte-collision, cp949 UHC syllables, 🚀 rejection) pass unchanged with OEM-based resolution.

`oxfmt` and `oxlint` clean on all touched files; `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` reports no errors in touched files (the 42 pre-existing errors on this machine reproduce identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout — local env, unrelated).

target.title: fix: keep channel auto-restart after abort race during backoff
target.body:
Closes #109659

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators would lose a channel permanently after a normal provider close when auto-restart backoff raced the dying run's abort signal. Gateway and container health checks stayed green while the channel never came back until a manual process restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel auto-restart now owns its own backoff abort lifecycle instead of sharing the dying run's `AbortSignal`. Intentional stops cancel that restart-owned supervisor, and abnormal exits clear `restartPending` with a diagnostic instead of an empty catch. No config, protocol, or public API changes.

## User Impact

When a channel connection drops, automatic restart remains reliable even if the previous run abort fires during backoff. Operators no longer need a manual gateway/container restart solely because the restart chain was swallowed silently. Intentional stops still cancel pending restarts.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox not used).

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts
# 51 passed

pnpm test:changed
# server-channels.test.ts 51 passed

pnpm format src/gateway/server-channels.ts src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts
# ok

oxlint src/gateway/server-channels.ts src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts
# 0 warnings, 0 errors

pnpm check:changed
# all local gates for touched files ok except Plugin SDK API baseline hash mismatch
# (docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256) — unrelated to this gateway-only diff
```

New/updated regression coverage:
- restart backoff sleep signal is not the dying run abort
- manual stop during backoff clears `restartPending`
- startAccount failure does not permanently kill the restart chain
- stop during restart-owned backoff clears pending without a second start

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: channel auto-restart no longer dies silently when abort races the restart backoff sleep; `restartPending` is reconciled and failures are logged
- Environment: local macOS, openclaw checkout at `fix/109659-channel-restart-abort-race`, focused Vitest gateway harness with fake timers and a stub channel plugin
- Current-main contrast: on main, `restart.next(abort.signal)` binds backoff to the dying run abort and `catch {}` swallows rejections, so a stop/abort during backoff can leave `restartPending: true` with no further `startChannelInternal` and no log. After this patch, backoff uses `restart.next()` (restart-owned signal only), `stopChannel` calls `restarts.get(rKey)?.cancel()`, and the catch path clears pending / logs failures
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts -t "does not bind auto-restart"`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts -t "does not auto-restart after manual stop"`
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts` (full suite for this file)
- Evidence after fix:
  - `does not bind auto-restart backoff to the dying run abort signal` — sleep signal !== run abort; second `startAccount` still runs after backoff
  - `does not auto-restart after manual stop during backoff` — still one start; `restartPending === false`
  - full file: **51 passed**
- Control check: sibling auto-restart cases (max attempts, stable-run reset, terminal disconnect, recovery stop timeout) still pass in the same file
- Observed result after fix: restart chain survives run-abort independence; intentional stop cancels restart-owned backoff and clears stuck pending instead of silent permanent unavailability
- What was not tested: live Zalo/`zalouser` multi-hour production outage, Docker healthcheck path, other channel providers beyond the shared manager harness

## AI disclosure

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok).

target.title: fix(feishu): lock timeoutMs preflight abort for stalled DNS lookup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu app registration goes through `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. Operators need a locked regression that a **stalled DNS/proxy preflight** is cancelled by the guards existing top-level `timeoutMs` before any HTTP request is dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper P1 on the prior tip: replacing `timeoutMs` with `AbortSignal.timeout()` does **not** add preflight protection — `fetchWithSsrFGuard` already converts `timeoutMs` into the preflight abort signal via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, and swapping owners only drops the shared `request timed out` diagnostic.

**This iteration (rebased on latest main):**
- Rebuilt on latest `main` (`22563878857`)
- **Kept** guard `timeoutMs` (no production ownership change)
- Added stalled-lookup regression next to the existing hang-POST timeout proof, matching its outcome shape
- The registration API (`FeishuAppRegistrationFetchOptions`) is unchanged on current main — test typechecks and passes as-is
- Existing SSRF guard tests already cover stalled-DNS timeout at the guard level (`fetch-guard.ssrf.test.ts:1916,1939`); this Feishu test validates the full `beginAppRegistration` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call chain

## User Impact

- **Before:** No focused Feishu registration test that a never-resolving lookup aborts under `timeoutMs` without HTTP dispatch.
- **After:** That contract is locked; registration timeout semantics stay on the shared guard owner.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `6d7aab253ee`
**Base:** `22563878857`

### Before / After comparison

| Dimension | Before (no stalled-DNS test) | After (this PR adds regression) |
|---|---|---|
| DNS lookup stall coverage | ❌ Not tested | ✅ `stalledLookup` (never-resolving Promise) → aborted by `timeoutMs` |
| HTTP dispatch during preflight | ❌ Not verified | ✅ `fetchSpy not.toHaveBeenCalled()` — locked |
| Error type on stall | ❌ Not verified | ✅ Must be `TimeoutError` |
| Error message on stall | ❌ Not verified | ✅ Must be `"request timed out"` — shared diagnostic preserved |
| Stall timeout window | ❌ Not verified | ✅ `elapsedMs ≥ 60 && < 2000` — quick abort, no hang |
| Existing POST timeout test | ✅ Covers TCP-accept-no-headers path | ✅ Unchanged, same outcome shape |

### Matched outcome shape (new test vs existing POST sibling)

| Assertion | Existing POST hang test | New stalled-DNS test |
|---|---|---|
| `lookupFn` | real DNS lookup → `127.0.0.1` | `stalledLookup` (never resolves) |
| abort mechanism | `timeoutMs` → preflight AbortSignal | `timeoutMs` → preflight AbortSignal |
| outcome | `TimeoutError` / `request timed out` | `TimeoutError` / `request timed out` |
| `fetchImpl` | reaches TCP listener | ❌ **not called** (never reaches HTTP) |
| elapsed window | ≥60ms, <2000ms | ≥60ms, <2000ms |

target.title: feat: trace Claude Code CLI model calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claude Code CLI turns did not emit trusted `model.call.started`, `model.call.completed`, and `model.call.error` diagnostics. Phoenix therefore could not show a useful model span with the OpenClaw-visible prompt, response, timing, and usage data for `claude-cli` runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add synthetic turn-level model-call tracing at the honest Claude Code CLI boundary for one-shot, managed persistent stdio, and paired-node execution. Each admitted attempt now receives exactly one terminal lifecycle event, including retry attempts, aborts, timeouts, process/parse failures, deferred background completion, persistence failure, and cleanup failure.

Content capture reuses the existing trusted capture policy and remains disabled by default. Granular capture includes only the effective OpenClaw prompt, OpenClaw-appended system prompt, and visible assistant blocks. It intentionally excludes Claude Code private prompts, hidden resume/compaction payloads, native tool schemas and arguments, raw Anthropic HTTP traffic, internal retries, upstream request IDs, and network TTFB.

Terminal cumulative usage, including cache read/write tokens, is used for the model span while existing last-assistant-message reply accounting remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators using OpenTelemetry/Phoenix can inspect a truthful Claude CLI model span with useful lifecycle, prompt/response, byte, timing, and aggregate usage data when content capture is explicitly enabled. Default installations remain metadata-only, and native OpenClaw/Codex tracing behavior is unchanged.

AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I reviewed the implementation and validation results.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-output.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.background-tasks.test.ts`: 3 files, 170 tests passed.

target.title: fix(video-generation): bound stalled video download response body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseWithLimit()` in video/music generation provider download paths capped `maxBytes` but omitted `chunkTimeoutMs`. A server that accepts the connection and then stops sending body chunks can leave the download Promise pending indefinitely, exhausting the Gateway connection pool under concurrent video downloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` on every video/music download path that was missing them, matching `google/video-generation-provider.ts` and `anthropic/usage.ts`. Resolve `ProviderOperationTimeoutMs` (`number | () => number`) to a concrete number before passing it to `chunkTimeoutMs` so TypeScript and the idle timer see a finite budget. Add a caller-path OpenAI regression that feeds a never-chunking `ReadableStream` body and asserts the production download error within the request deadline.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled upstream video/music download body could hang the provider download forever.

**After:** Download body reads fail closed after the operation idle budget with a clear `…download stalled: no data received for Nms` error, releasing the connection.

## Changed Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `chunkTimeoutMs` via `resolveOpenAIVideoDownloadTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/byteplus/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `resolveBytePlusVideoDownloadTimeoutMs` + `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |
| `extensions/runway/video-generation-provider.ts` | Add `resolveRunwayVideoDownloadTimeoutMs` + `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` |

target.title: fix(ui): usage overview hints do not open when clicked
target.body: AI-assisted: Codex was used to investigate and implement this fix. I reviewed the resulting code and validation evidence. ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where users clicking any of the nine `?` hints in Control UI **Usage → Usage Overview** would not see the explanatory content. The hints were passive native-title spans, so their content was not reliably available to click, touch, or keyboard users. ## Why This Change Was Made The overview hints are now focusable buttons backed by Web Awesome tooltips with stable target IDs. target.title: fix: tighten processSchema offset/limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer

## Summary

**Problem**: `processSchema.offset` and `processSchema.limit` accept floating-point values via `Type.Number()`, but both are inherently integer fields (line offset, line count). Float values like `offset=1.5` are silently truncated at runtime, creating an LLM intent mismatch.

**Solution**: Tighten both fields to `Type.Integer()` — the schema layer now rejects floats before they reach runtime. Negative values are preserved at the schema level (no `minimum: 0` constraint) and normalized by the existing runtime guard in `sliceLogLines` (`Math.max(0, Math.floor(offset))`).

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707
## Summary

Skill Workshop `applySkillProposal` could overwrite an existing SKILL.md with plan-only proposal content without validation or recovery. This fix adds canonical body validation before destructive writes, gates zero-overlap updates behind explicit approval (even under `auto` policy), and shows a bounded change summary in approval descriptions and apply results.

- Problem: `applySkillProposal` wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation; plan/change-description proposals silently overwrote real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) made this happen without user confirmation.
- Solution: Validate proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser (not heading heuristics), reject empty bodies, gate zero-overlap updates behind `requiresExplicitApproval` which forces pending approval even under `auto` policy, add `computeSkillChangeSummary` for `+N/-M lines` summaries, and document `rollback.json` restore path in troubleshooting.
- What changed: `src/skills/workshop/service.ts` (canonical validation + approval flag + summary), `src/skills/workshop/policy.ts` (zero-overlap forces pending approval), `src/skills/workshop/types.ts` (`changeSummary` + `requiresExplicitApproval` fields), `src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.ts` (apply result text), `src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts` (6 lifecycle proof tests), `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md` (troubleshooting entries)
- What did NOT change: Generation prompts (already fixed in PR #108339), `scanProposalBundle`, `readProposalFrontmatter`, proposal frontmatter schema, rollback write logic, any config/env surface, the `proposeCreateSkill`/`proposeUpdateSkill` entry points

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #107707
- Related #107690 (auto-approval policy change that amplified the risk)
- Related #108339 (generation-side prompt hardening, separate from this apply-side fix)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The default `approvalPolicy` change from `pending` to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. The initial patch used heading-presence and exact-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that heading checks block valid headingless skills (the documented SKILL.md contract only requires frontmatter + markdown body, not a body heading) and that single-line overlap is trivially bypassable, while zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Plan-only or unrelated proposal bodies overwriting SKILL.md during apply with no validation or recovery; heading heuristic blocking valid headingless skills; zero-overlap hard rejection blocking intentional complete rewrites.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 24, branch `fix/apply-body-validation-107707`, SHA `3a45f07899`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts --run
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts --run

 RUN  v4.1.10 /home/0668001188/github/20260716-2/openclaw

 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts (41 tests) 11195ms
     ✓ applies a zero-overlap update with requiresExplicitApproval flag  465ms
     ✓ applies a plan-only update proposal with requiresExplicitApproval (no body overlap)  532ms
     ✓ rejects an empty proposal body during apply  491ms
     ✓ applies a valid headingless skill update without requiresExplicitApproval  427ms
     ✓ applies a valid full-content update and records rollback for restoration  500ms
     ✓ applies a copied-one-line plan with requiresExplicitApproval  533ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  41 passed (41)
```

Matrix evidence (apply-path validation behavior):

```
Proposal body form                              => Result
Empty body (whitespace only)                    => Hard rejection: "Proposal body is empty"
Invalid frontmatter (plan/description only)     => Hard rejection: "does not contain valid SKILL.md frontmatter"
Zero overlap with current SKILL.md              => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=true, forced pending approval
Valid headingless skill with shared content     => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false
Valid full-content update with shared lines     => Apply succeeds, changeSummary returned
Copied-one-line plan (heading matches)          => Apply succeeds, requiresExplicitApproval=false (overlap detected)
```

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected before SKILL.md is touched
2. Proposals without valid frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected
3. Zero-overlap updates (unrelated replacement or plan) apply with `requiresExplicitApproval=true` and are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy
4. Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) apply normally without `requiresExplicitApproval`
5. Valid full-content updates with shared lines apply normally with `changeSummary`
6. SKILL.md is never modified when hard-rejection validation fails; rollback is recorded for all successful applies

## Root Cause

`applySkillProposal` in `src/skills/workshop/service.ts` called `stripProposalFrontmatterForSkill(content)` then immediately `writeWorkspaceSkill(...)` with no validation of the resulting body content. `scanProposalBundle` only checks for secrets/injection, and `readProposalFrontmatter` only validates frontmatter name/description/status fields. The content body — the part that becomes SKILL.md — had zero validation. Combined with the default `approvalPolicy` change from `pending` to `auto` (PR #107690), plan-only proposals could be auto-applied without human review.

## Regression Test Plan

- `src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts`: 6 new tests covering empty body, invalid frontmatter, zero-overlap approval gate, headingless skill, valid apply + rollback, and copied-one-line plan
- All 35 existing tests still pass (no regressions)
- `src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts`: 8 existing tests pass

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- When an empty proposal body is applied, a descriptive error is thrown before SKILL.md is touched
- When a proposal without valid SKILL.md frontmatter is applied, a descriptive error is thrown before SKILL.md is touched
- When a zero-overlap update proposal is applied under `auto` policy, it is forced through pending approval instead of being silently auto-applied
- When a zero-overlap update is applied (after approval), the result includes `requiresExplicitApproval: true`
- When a valid update proposal is applied, the approval description shows `Changes: +N lines, -M lines`
- Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) are no longer blocked

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: 6 lifecycle proof tests pass; existing 35 tests unchanged and pass
- Edge cases checked: empty body, plan-only body (zero overlap), headingless skill, copied-one-line plan, valid update with shared content, intentional complete rewrite (zero overlap + approval)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — headingless skills that were previously blocked by the heading heuristic now work; zero-overlap updates that were previously hard-rejected now go through approval gate; valid proposals with shared content continue to work unchanged
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — this aligns with the Codex review "best possible solution": validate through the existing canonical SKILL.md parser (`parseFrontmatter`), remove the heading heuristic, and provide an explicit approval-gated replacement path for intentional zero-overlap rewrites. Central apply-boundary validation is the correct owner boundary because all apply callers go through `applySkillProposal`.
- **Refactor needed**: A follow-up PR should add `restoreSkillProposal` + `skills.proposals.restore` Gateway method + CLI command. Current PR documents the manual restore path via `rollback.json` as the minimum viable solution.
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Rejecting proposals at `scanProposalBundle` time — rejected because the scanner checks secrets/injection, not content structure. (2) Heading heuristic — rejected because the documented SKILL.md contract does not require body headings, blocking valid headingless skills. (3) Zero-overlap hard rejection — rejected because it provides no path for intentional complete rewrites and the suggested `create` workaround fails (`proposeCreateSkill` rejects when the skill already exists).

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1 (iCodemate)
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #107707 analysis; Codex review P1 findings implementation

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest-risk area**: The `requiresExplicitApproval` zero-overlap detection uses exact-line matching via `Set<string>`, which may flag intentional rewrites of very short skills (1-2 lines) where no original lines survive.
- **Mitigation**: Zero-overlap updates are not rejected — they are gated behind explicit approval, preserving the replacement path. The operator can approve the intentional rewrite. For `auto` policy, zero-overlap forces a pending approval, which is the safe default for destructive writes with no content overlap.
- **Compatibility impact**: Backward compatible — headingless skills now work (previously blocked); zero-overlap updates go through approval gate (previously hard-rejected with no workaround); valid proposals with shared content work unchanged.

target.title: refactor: separate external conversations from local sessions
target.body:
Closes #108666

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where agents could confuse a local model session with the external conversation attached to it. This was especially visible with Reef: a message intended for another agent could loop into the sender's local session, and waiting for a remote reply required brittle channel-target reasoning.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates stable external `conversationRef` addresses from local session context. It adds owner-only conversation discovery, durable fire-and-forget sends, and reply-correlated turns owned by the Gateway; transports remain channel plugins, while generic delivery, queue recovery, idempotency, and reply capture live in core.

The refactor also makes Reef use one process-wide live runtime, reserves its message ID before durable queueing, and consumes an exact correlated reply inline without starting a second local agent turn. Unsolicited messages and replies that arrive after process restart continue through ordinary inbound dispatch.

The agent-scoped lease and conversation-delivery additions are combined in the unshipped v11 schema. Released pre-v11 databases migrate once into that canonical shape; no v12 schema is introduced.

## User Impact

Agents can now use `conversations_list`, `conversations_send`, and `conversations_turn` instead of treating session keys as remote destinations. Reef conversations behave like real external conversations: sends survive Gateway recovery, exact replies return to the calling tool, unrelated inbound messages still start normal turns, and multi-agent operation IDs cannot collide in the shared queue.

## Evidence

- Final head `21cc14e3568076221835ed65503bf25154f891e9`: fresh two-pass whole-branch autoreview, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxq85t2sa55j6jm48taq25kc`: all 35 changed test files passed across 11 Vitest shards, covering the v11 migration, conversation tools, Gateway RPCs, durable outbound recovery, reply capture, and Reef transport.

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): keep blank credentials from overriding AWS auth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Amazon Bedrock users could lose access to the AWS default credential chain when `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, or `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` was present but contained only whitespace. In the bearer-token case, OpenClaw selected bearer authentication and the AWS SDK emitted an unusable whitespace authorization header. In the static-key case, the AWS SDK's `fromEnv()` provider treats whitespace strings as truthy and selects them before profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials, blocking the default chain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock now trims explicit and environment-provided bearer tokens before selecting bearer authentication, treats blank static credential environment values as absent when deciding whether to refresh shared AWS configuration, and clears blank static credential env vars before the BedrockRuntimeClient resolves credentials at runtime so the SDK default chain can fall through to profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS.

The AWS SDK `fromEnv()` provider in `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node` checks only truthiness (not trimmed content), so `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=" "` is accepted as a valid credential and prevents the chain from advancing. Clearing blank env vars before client creation lets the chain reach profile/SSO/ECS/IMDS credentials.

## User Impact

Users with accidentally blank Bedrock credential environment variables can continue using valid AWS profile, SSO, or default-chain credentials. Valid bearer tokens are still supported and are normalized before being passed to the AWS SDK.

## Evidence

- Direct production-path reproduction on Linux / Node 24.18.0: before the fix, `streamBedrock` configured the AWS client with `{"token":{"token":"   "},"authSchemePreference":["httpBearerAuth"]}` for a whitespace-only bearer token.
- Direct AWS SDK request capture before network I/O: `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` produced `Authorization: Bearer    ` from that configuration.
- After the fix, the same `streamBedrock` path configured no token provider for whitespace-only input; `"  valid-token  "` produced `{ "token": "valid-token" }`.
- `sanitizeBlankAwsCredentials` clears blank `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`/`AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` from process.env before the Bedrock client resolves credentials, allowing the SDK default chain to reach profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/aws-credential-refresh.test.ts` — 48 tests passed.
- Mutation check: restoring the previous truthiness checks made assertions fail (blank runtime token, token trimming, shared-config refresh, and blank static key sanitization cases); restoring this patch returned all 48 tests to green.
- `git diff --check` passed.

AI-assisted. I reviewed the runtime, discovery, refresh, embedding, and core AWS-auth sibling paths, plus the exact `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime@3.1078.0` auth configuration, `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node` default chain `fromEnv()` behavior, and Smithy bearer signer contract.

target.title: fix(parallels): keep host server stderr tails UTF-8 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Parallels host artifact server startup diagnostics could show replacement characters when the bounded stderr tail started in the middle of a UTF-8 character. It also avoids losing a multibyte character when the process stream splits that character across chunks.

Related independent bug-family PRs: this PR and #109669 both keep byte-bounded diagnostic tails UTF-8 safe. They touch separate script helpers and are not stacked; either can merge first.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host server startup path now retains stderr as a bounded raw byte tail and decodes it only when formatting the failure message. That preserves byte caps, keeps split UTF-8 sequences reconstructable across chunks, and drops only leading continuation bytes after truncation.

## User Impact

Developers debugging Parallels smoke setup failures get readable stderr tails instead of corrupted UTF-8 at the diagnostic boundary.

target.title: fix(music): stop hanging when generated asset downloads drip forever
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where music generation providers (e.g. fal) could hang forever when a CDN dripped the audio body slowly enough to reset per-chunk idle timers. `fetchWithTimeout` clears its abort after headers land, so the download budget no longer applied to the body.

Additionally:
1. Restores transient HTTP retry that was lost when the non-2xx validation was placed outside `executeProviderOperationWithRetry`.
2. Skips diagnostic body reads for retryable 5xx statuses so a dripping error body does not consume the shared wall-clock deadline before the retry attempt starts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three changes in `downloadGeneratedMusicAsset`:

1. **Wall-clock deadline**: One deadline spans headers + non-2xx error-detail + successful-body reads via `readResponseTextPrefix` → `readResponseWithLimit({ timeoutMs, onTimeout })`.

2. **Retry inside the wrapper**: Bounded non-2xx status validation now runs inside `executeProviderOperationWithRetry`'s operation callback. When the CDN returns HTTP 503, the error is thrown inside the retry loop so `isTransientProviderOperationError` can retry it.

3. **Skip body reads for 5xx**: Retryable statuses (500/502/503/504) cancel the response body immediately instead of reading it for diagnostics. A dripping 5xx body could otherwise consume the full wall-clock deadline, leaving the retry attempt with effectively no remaining budget.

Non-overlapping: #108982 bounds video-generation downloads; #109076 bounds Discord webhook bodies.

## User Impact

- Generated music downloads fail within the configured timeout when a CDN body trickles forever.
- Transient CDN errors (503, etc.) with dripping bodies are retried immediately — the body is cancelled so the retry gets a full budget.
- Non-retryable errors (400, etc.) still include bounded diagnostic detail.
- Music generation no longer sticks forever on a slow-drip CDN response.

## Evidence

Exact head: `dee8f741c1da3899930e3602cf858d0e6072632d`

`oxfmt --check src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ bounds a dripping download body with one wall-clock deadline 284ms
 ✓ throws on non-2xx HTTP status without retry 18ms
 ✓ retries on transient HTTP status before succeeding 268ms
 ✓ skips diagnostic body read on retryable status so deadline survives for retry 264ms
 ✓ does not bound a dripping body when only chunk idle timeout is used 410ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

- **Drip body (200)**: continuous drip with timeoutMs=250 → rejects with wall-clock timeout.
- **Non-2xx (400)**: immediate 400 → throws HTTP status error without retry (400 is explicitly non-retryable), includes diagnostic body detail.
- **Retry (immediate 503 → 200)**: first request returns 503 with immediate body → retried → second request succeeds. Proves `requestCount === 2`.
- **Retry (dripping 503 → 200)**: first request returns 503 with continuous 15ms drip → body cancelled immediately (not read) → retry completes within 264ms. Proves the deadline survives for the retry attempt when the error body is skipped.
- **Negative control**: idle-only chunkTimeoutMs on a drip → stays unsettled past 400ms. Proves old code path has no wall-clock bound.

### Mutation check

Without fix (stash provider-assets.ts): `retries on transient` FAIL — 503 not retried.
With fix restored: `retries on transient` PASS — `requestCount === 2`.

### Not tested

Live fal CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: refactor: move non-session runtime journals to SQLite
target.body:
Related: #98236

AI-assisted: yes. The complete branch diff was reviewed with the repo autoreview workflow; all findings were addressed before publication.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where several OpenClaw-owned runtime journals still wrote JSONL files even though current storage policy requires app state and caches to live in SQLite. Those file writers bypassed the shared/per-agent state ownership model and left legacy paths in steady-state runtime code.

The session/transcript store was deliberately excluded because #98236 owns that completed SQLite flip.

## Why This Change Was Made

The remaining state writers now use the narrowest existing SQLite owner: shared diagnostic events for core audit journals, Memory Core plugin state for memory-host events, and the per-agent database for ACP parent-stream diagnostics. Legacy persistent audit/event files import only through explicit `openclaw doctor --fix` migrations; audit imports require exclusive state ownership, verify SQLite rows, sanitize the retired source, and only then archive it. ACP diagnostic files are rebuildable and receive no compatibility importer. There are no runtime fallback readers or dual writes.

### Audit classification

| Surface | Observed role | Policy classification | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/config/io.audit.ts` (`logs/config-audit.jsonl`) | Core config-write/observe audit writer | Shared state DB, `diagnostic_events` / `config-audit` | Migrated; redacted records; bounded to latest 50,000 rows; legacy import and archive owned by doctor only |
| `src/system-agent/audit.ts` (`audit/system-agent.jsonl`, retired Crestodian path) | Core system-agent mutation audit writer | Shared state DB, `diagnostic_events` / `system-agent-audit` | Migrated; bounded to latest 50,000 rows; legacy import and archive owned by doctor only |
| `src/memory-host-sdk/events.ts` (`memory/.dreams/events.jsonl`) | Memory recall/promotion/dream event state consumed by status, public artifacts, and Memory Wiki | Memory Core plugin KV in shared SQLite | Migrated with per-workspace append ordering; doctor imports legacy source lines ahead of SQLite-native events; public artifact is now a virtual JSON artifact backed by SQLite |
| `src/agents/acp-spawn-parent-stream.ts` (`*.acp-stream.jsonl`) | Child-session ACP parent-stream diagnostic state | Per-agent DB, `acp_parent_stream_events` | Migrated; rows are session-owned and cascade on session deletion; writes batch synchronously, retry with backoff, and cap pending diagnostics; old transient files are not imported |
| `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts` | Reads legacy/archive transcript JSONL; rollups already use per-agent SQLite | Excluded session/transcript area; no JSONL writer | Left unchanged; #98236 owns session/transcript storage |
| `src/security/fix.ts` | Repairs permissions on excluded transcript artifacts | Excluded session/transcript maintenance; no writer | Left unchanged |
| `src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.ts` | Names/filter rules inside backup production | Named backup artifact | Left unchanged |
| `src/agents/cache-trace.ts`, `src/agents/anthropic-payload-log.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.raw-stream.ts`, `src/logging/diagnostic-*`, channel delivery trace | Explicit opt-in traces, raw provider capture, or support bundles | Named diagnostic/log artifacts | Left unchanged |
| CLI runner/Claude session files, transcript/session-manager paths, hooks, compaction checkpoints, session inspection/branching | Provider/external-tool contracts or the excluded session/transcript surface | External tool contract or #98236-owned session artifact | Left unchanged |
| `src/trajectory/{runtime-file,paths,cleanup,types}.ts` | SQLite runtime plus explicit trajectory export/legacy discovery | Named export artifact; no steady-state JSONL app-state writer | Left unchanged |
| `src/infra/{exec-host,exec-approvals}.ts` and node CLI JSONL references | Framed IPC/socket payloads | External wire contract, not file state | Left unchanged |
| `src/plugin-sdk/api-baseline.ts` | Generated SDK inspection output | Generated developer artifact | Left unchanged; tracked checksum regenerated for this SDK surface |
| Schema/help/status/tool-display/workshop references and test-support/harness files from discovery | Format names, readers, fixtures, or temporary external/session scratch | No remaining production file writer | Left unchanged |

The post-change discovery still finds legacy migration constants and legitimate artifact/wire/session references, but no additional non-session OpenClaw-owned runtime JSONL writer.

## User Impact

Operators get one SQLite-backed ownership model for these journals, deterministic cleanup with session deletion, bounded audit retention, and explicit doctor repair for persistent legacy files. Existing backup, support-bundle, provider-log, export, and wire-format artifacts keep their documented behavior.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox focused validation: 689 tests across audit storage/migration, config audit, system-agent audit, ACP spawn/stream storage, memory-host events/public artifacts/doctor migration, Memory Wiki, and the database-first policy guard.
- `pnpm check:changed`: conflict markers, format, generated baselines, SDK API/surface, package exports, deprecated API usage, plugin boundaries, package guards, core/core-test/extension/extension-test/root typechecks all passed. Full core lint found five task-local mechanical issues; all were fixed, then targeted lint and the three affected test shards (62 tests) passed.

target.title: fix(ci): bound opengrep installer downloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Both OpenGrep CI workflows streamed the pinned installer directly from `curl` into Bash. Current `main` now bounds those transfers through #109576, but Bash can still execute a partial response before curl reaches its deadline and fails the pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Download the pinned installer completely into `RUNNER_TEMP` with explicit connection and total-transfer deadlines, then execute it only after curl succeeds. This matches the existing OpenShell installer contract while preserving the OpenGrep commit pin and `-v "$OPENGREP_VERSION"` invocation.

The rebase onto current `main` also folded #109576's simpler timeout-only guard into one stronger regression test, avoiding duplicate policy tests.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. OpenGrep PR-diff and full-scan jobs fail cleanly on a stalled or incomplete installer response instead of hanging or executing partial installer bytes.

## Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI sidebar splits scrolling across two nested regions: the pinned nav block caps at 60% height with its own hidden scrollbar, and only the session list actually scrolls, so pinned nav permanently eats vertical space. The scrollbar also sits ~10px inside the draggable resize divider, floating detached from the edge it belongs to. New-thread affordances are scattered (Sessions-header plus, agent-chip plus, macOS titlebar plus only while collapsed, logo click), and on macOS the titlebar search/new-thread buttons vanish whenever the sidebar is expanded. The update card is a chunky two-line banner in an otherwise slim footer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- One scroller for nav + sessions (`.sidebar-shell__body`): only the brand row and footer stay pinned. Deletes the desktop 60% nav cap and the mobile drawer's duplicate of it; scroll-fade masks and scroll-state tracking move up to the body.
- The scrollbar hugs the drag divider: the body cancels the shell's horizontal padding via a shared `--sidebar-pad-x` so the two values cannot drift (desktop 10px, drawer 16/14px).
- New-thread moves next to search in the brand row (disabled while disconnected, same semantics as the removed Sessions-header plus). The agent-scoped plus on the footer chip stays; the Sessions header keeps only sort.
- macOS web-chrome hosts show search + new-thread in the titlebar permanently next to back/forward (previously only while the sidebar was collapsed). target.title: test: session freshness fixtures flake near the daily-reset boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a time-of-day CI flake: `src/commands/agent.session.test.ts` freshness scenarios seed session timestamps relative to `Date.now()`. When a CI run starts within ~70 seconds after the 04:00 local daily-reset boundary, the seeded session-start falls before the boundary, the resolver correctly rolls a new session, and the "reuse" scenarios fail. This flaked `checks-node-compact-large-1` on unrelated PRs tonight (runs starting 04:00:33 UTC).

## Why This Change Was Made

The failure is deterministic when the clock sits just past the boundary (reproduced on a clean main checkout with a forced clock: `TZ=UTC` + `Date.now` pinned to `04:00:30Z` fails identically). Tests should not depend on the wall clock's position relative to the reset boundary.

## User Impact

None at runtime — test-only. CI stops failing spuriously for ~70 seconds every day per timezone.

## Evidence

- Pinned local noon (faking only `Date`, real timers restored per test): file passes in `TZ=UTC`, `TZ=Etc/GMT+2`, and `TZ=Asia/Kathmandu`, and under the exact boundary repro (`Date.now` forced to `2026-07-17T04:00:30Z`): 7/7 in all four runs.

target.title: feat(onboarding): recommend plugins and skills from installed apps
target.body:
# What Problem This Solves

New users finish onboarding with a bare install even when their Mac is full of apps
OpenClaw already has plugins and skills for (Notion, Obsidian, Slack, 1Password,
Things, …). Nothing connects "what is installed on this machine" with "what OpenClaw
can do with it", so discovery is manual catalog browsing.

# Why This Change Was Made

Adds installed-app plugin/skill recommendations to `openclaw onboard`:

1. **Scan** — enumerate `/Applications`, `~/Applications`, and a small allowlist of
   `/System/Applications` (TCC-free: no permission dialog can fire — `readdir`,
   Launch Services, and Spotlight metadata are unprotected paths; verified on a real
   machine).
2. **Candidates** — loose name matches from the official plugin/channel/provider
   catalogs plus top-3 ClawHub skill search hits per app (concurrency 4, 5s/request,
   20s overall budget; failures degrade to catalog-only candidates).
3. **AI matching** — one completion on the model route the wizard just verified. The
   model receives app names + candidate descriptions and returns genuine matches with
   a tier (`recommended`/`optional`) and a short reason. No curated bundle-id map to
   maintain; the model rejects coincidental name overlaps (naive matching paired
   Linear→`line`, Zed→`zededa`, Parallels→`parallel` in prototyping — the live test
   asserts these traps stay dead).
4. **Consent surface** — the wizard step is deliberately "magical" (product decision):
   no consent prompt before the scan, but the scanning progress line and the results
   note both disclose that app names are matched using the configured model and
   ClawHub search, and `wizard.appRecommendations: false` disables the feature
   entirely. The results step lists detected apps and installs only what the user
   selects (recommended tier pre-checked, explicit skip).
5. **Remote gateway path** — the TS node-host gains the `device.apps` invoke command
   Android already ships (same envelope; macOS emits `label`/`bundleId` where Android
   emits `label`/`packageName`). Node-side sharing is **off by default** (privacy
   parity with Android's consent toggle) via node-host config /
   `--share-installed-apps`; disabled invokes return the typed
   `INSTALLED_APPS_SHARING_DISABLED` error. The gateway allowlists the command for
   macOS nodes and strips it everywhere when the kill switch is off. Local onboarding
   scans directly and does not use the node command.

Also fixes a latent bug this feature exposed: `runSetupInferenceTest` applied the
32-token verification-probe output cap (`SETUP_INFERENCE_TEST_MAX_TOKENS`) to every
completion, so any custom prompt longer than a few words returned a reasoning-only
turn and "Agent couldn't generate a response." Custom-prompt completions now use the
model's own output budget; the probe keeps its cap.

Prior art: Setapp is the only mainstream product doing install-scan → recommendation;
its trust framing (scan silently, show the detected list, act opt-in) is what this
follows, with explicit disclosure because app names do leave the machine.

# User Impact

- `openclaw onboard` (non-quickstart, macOS, working model route) gains one optional
  step: detected apps → tiered multiselect → install. Zero matches or any failure
  (offline ClawHub, model error, malformed model output) skips the step silently;
  onboarding never blocks on this feature.
- New config key `wizard.appRecommendations` (default enabled) to disable.
- Mac/headless nodes can opt in to sharing their app inventory with the gateway
  (`--share-installed-apps`, persisted in node-host config, default off).

# Evidence

- **Live end-to-end test** (real ClawHub `/api/v1/search` + real OpenAI
  `gpt-5.6-luna`): `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 OPENAI_API_KEY=… pnpm test:live
  src/system-agent/setup-app-recommendations.live.test.ts` — **passed** (76s). Fixture
  inventory of 9 real apps incl. traps; model matched Notion→`notion`,
  Obsidian→`obsidian`, Slack→`slack-api`, Linear→`linear`, Things→`things-mac`,
  1Password→`1password` and produced none of the trap pairings.
- **Unit tests** (all passing): scanner fixtures/filtering/sorting + Linux-safe plist
  reader injection; candidate dedupe + ClawHub failure degradation; matcher zod
  filtering incl. fenced-JSON/extra-key/overlong-reason tolerance; node `device.apps`
  gating + Android-parity envelope; gateway allowlist + kill-switch stripping;
  node-host config persistence; wizard gating/pre-check/skip/install paths
  (`pnpm test src/infra/installed-apps.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-app-recommendations.test.ts
  src/node-host/invoke-device-apps.test.ts src/node-host/runtime.test.ts
  src/node-host/config.test.ts src/wizard/setup.app-recommendations.test.ts
  src/gateway/node-command-policy.test.ts src/wizard/setup.test.ts
  src/system-agent/setup-inference.test.ts`).
- `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm config:schema:check`, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `git diff --check` —
  all green.
- Autoreview (Codex, gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): two accepted findings fixed (Linux CI
  plutil dependency in the scanner test; unbounded ClawHub phase → 20s budget). The
  remaining consent-first finding is consciously rejected as the documented product
  decision (default-on with disclosure + kill switch); an inline comment records it.
- Real-machine scan prototype: 45/52 apps matched, no TCC prompt, <2s.

target.title: fix(browser): keep tab reachability retry delay abortable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cancelling a browser tab operation during the reachability retry delay would wait the full delay before responding to the cancellation.

`ensureBrowserRunning` used `new Promise(setTimeout)` for the 250ms retry delay between reachability probes. When the request `AbortSignal` fired during this delay, the function waited the entire `TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS` before calling `signal.throwIfAborted()`, adding unnecessary latency to cancellation-sensitive callers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry delay now uses `sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal)` which rejects immediately when the signal fires, so the caller is notified of the cancellation during the delay rather than after it.

Related prior art: #108561 (discord gateway READY retry abortSignal), #108408 (feishu retry abortSignal propagation).

## User Impact

Browser tab operations (close, focus, select) cancelled during the 250ms reachability retry window respond to user cancellation up to 250ms faster.

## Evidence

### Scope

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Head | `eac9fd9a2f5` |
| Files | `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.ts` (+4/−5) · `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts` (+1/−1) |
| Net | +5 / −6 across 2 files |

### Production change (behavior)

```ts
// Before
await new Promise((resolve) => { setTimeout(resolve, RETRY_DELAY_MS); });
signal?.throwIfAborted();

// After
await sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal);
```

### Real-timer timing proof

A standalone Node.js script (`scripts/proof-109536-abort-timing.mjs`) compares the two patterns with real `performance.now()` timers and a real `AbortController`. Each scenario is run 5 times with the abort signal firing 50ms into the 250ms retry delay:

```
--- BEFORE (old code) ---
  Run 1: 250.6 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 2: 250.8 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 3: 250.3 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 4: 251.0 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 5: 250.2 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)

--- AFTER (new code: sleepWithAbort) ---
  Run 1: 50.5 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 2: 50.6 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 3: 50.5 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 4: 51.0 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 5: 50.8 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
```

- **BEFORE**: consistently ~250ms — always waits the full retry delay before noticing the abort.
- **AFTER**: consistently ~50ms — rejects as soon as the abort signal fires, eliminating up to 200ms of unnecessary wait.

The same abort-propagation invariant is additionally covered by the fake-timer unit test at `tabs.test.ts:345`.

### Local gates (touched surface)

| Gate | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts` | **22 passed** / 1 file |

### Proof

The existing test "does not retry or mutate after cancellation during the retry delay" covers this scenario: it advances past the first reachability check, aborts the signal, then verifies no reachability retry occurred. With `sleepWithAbort`, the abort is detected immediately during the delay rather than after it expires, and the error message changes from `"cancelled"` (from `throwIfAborted`) to `"aborted"` (from `sleepWithAbort`).

Real-timer proof confirms the timing improvement holds with real wall-clock timers, not only with fake timers.

---

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(plugins): accept npm 12 json shapes in install metadata reads
target.body:
Fixes #109550.

## What Problem This Solves

npm 12 changed the `--json` output shapes of `npm view` and `npm pack`:

- `npm view <spec> ... --json` now wraps the result in a **singleton array** (`[{...}]`) instead of a bare object.
- `npm pack <spec> --json` now returns an **object keyed by package name** (`{"openclaw": {...}}`) instead of an entry array (`[{...}]`).

The install metadata readers assumed the npm ≤11 shapes, so on npm 12:

- `resolveNpmPackArchiveMetadata` fails closed with `npm pack metadata read produced incomplete package metadata` (the wrapper object is normalized as if it were an entry, producing empty metadata).
- `packNpmSpecToArchive` succeeds but silently returns `metadata: {}`, so plugin install/update flows lose the resolved name/version/integrity.
- Worker release verification (`verifyPublishedNpmRelease`) rejects published packages: the npm 12 view array fails `parseNpmPackageIdentity`, and the name-keyed pack object fails the array check, ending in `npm pack returned incomplete worker package metadata`.

This is what users hit as `openclaw update` / `openclaw plugins install` failing with incomplete-metadata errors on npm 12 (#109550).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both call sites need the same normalization, so it lives in one shared resolver (`resolveNpmJsonEntries` in `src/infra/npm-registry-spec.ts`, next to the other npm registry contract helpers) instead of two local copies. The resolver keeps the npm ≤11 shapes working unchanged and unwraps the npm 12 singleton array / name-keyed object only when the value does not itself look like an entry (`id`/`name`/`version`/`filename` present), so a package legitimately named like a wrapper key cannot be mistaken for one.

## Changes

- `src/infra/npm-registry-spec.ts`: add exported `resolveNpmJsonEntries(value)` that passes arrays through, keeps bare entry objects as single entries, and unwraps npm 12 name-keyed wrapper objects into their entry values.
- `src/infra/install-source-utils.ts`: `parseNpmPackJsonOutput` now resolves entries via the shared resolver, fixing both `packNpmSpecToArchive` and `resolveNpmPackArchiveMetadata` on npm 12.
- `src/gateway/worker-environments/bundle.ts`: `verifyPublishedNpmRelease` unwraps the `npm view` singleton array and the `npm pack` name-keyed object through the same resolver before identity parsing.
- Regression tests: `resolveNpmJsonEntries` shape table (npm ≤11 array, bare object, npm 12 singleton array, npm 12 name-keyed object, scoped name key, junk passthrough), plus npm 12 pack-shape cases for `packNpmSpecToArchive` and `resolveNpmPackArchiveMetadata`.

## User Impact

Users on npm 12 can install and update plugins and gateway packages again; metadata (name/version/resolvedSpec/integrity) is read correctly from both npm 12 output shapes. Behavior on npm ≤11 is unchanged (verified against a real npm 10.9.4 below). No config, migration, or API changes.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/npm-registry-spec.test.ts src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/bundle.test.ts` — 93/93 passed on Node 22.22.0.
- Real npm 12 driver proof below (real `npm@12.0.1` binary + real registry + real `openclaw-2026.7.1.tgz`), before/after this patch.
- Real npm 10.9.4 regression run: identical correct metadata after the patch (no behavior change for npm ≤11).
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files. `tsgo` core lane reports only pre-existing `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` errors from a stale local dependency install; the changed files are clean.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** On npm 12, plugin/gateway install metadata reads failed with `npm pack metadata read produced incomplete package metadata` or silently returned empty metadata because `npm pack --json` output is keyed by package name and `npm view --json` output is a singleton array instead of the npm ≤11 shapes.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0, real `npm@12.0.1` binary (installed via `npm install --prefix /tmp/npm12-test npm@12`), real npmjs.org registry, real published `openclaw-2026.7.1.tgz`, plus real `npm@10.9.4` as the npm ≤11 baseline. Current head: `df3783503fb204166f6c80190a93db58fa4b0668`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `PATH="/tmp/npm12-test/node_modules/.bin:$PATH" node --import tsx /tmp/npm12-proof/proof.mts`, where the driver imports the production functions from `src/infra/install-source-utils.js` and calls `resolveNpmPackArchiveMetadata({ archivePath: "/tmp/npm12-test/openclaw-2026.7.1.tgz" })` and `packNpmSpecToArchive({ spec: "is-odd@3.0.1", timeoutMs: 60_000, cwd })`, spawning the real npm 12 subprocess and reading the real tarball back from disk.

**Evidence after fix:** Before the patch (same driver, base revision): `resolveNpmPackArchiveMetadata => {"ok":false,"error":"npm pack metadata read produced incomplete package metadata"}` and `packNpmSpecToArchive => {"ok":true,...,"metadata":{}}`. target.title: fix(tlon): bound Urbit auth response body drain to prevent OOM
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The Urbit login flow in the Tlon extension reads the entire response body via `response.text()` solely to flush the stream so that `set-cookie` headers finalize. The body content is discarded. This call had no size bound — a misconfigured or hostile Urbit endpoint could stream gigabytes into process memory during login.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the unbounded `response.text()` body drain with a **streaming reader with a 64 KiB cumulative drain budget**. When the body stream is available (Node 18+, Bun, Deno), the reader reads chunks until the total drained bytes reach the threshold, then cancels the stream. The 64 KiB threshold is a **cumulative accounting cap** — a single producer chunk may push the total above 64 KiB because we check after each read, which avoids splitting chunks mid-stream. When no body stream is available (rare polyfill/edge case), the fallback `text()` path is preserved for compatibility.

The body content was always discarded; only the `set-cookie` header is consumed.

## User Impact

Urbit login no longer risks OOM from an oversized response body. Normal login flows (small JSON bodies) are completely unaffected. The cookie extraction behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/auth.ssrf.test.ts --run`: **5/5 passed** (2 existing SSRF + 3 new body drain tests).
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- The three new tests cover: streamed body drain with cookie extraction, oversized stream cancellation after the 64 KiB cap, and the body-less fallback path.

### Real behavior proof (loopback drain)

Controlled loopback exercising the same drain pattern used in production:

```json
{"case":"under-cap","drained":1024,"cancelled":false,"cookie":"urbauth-~zod=abc; Path=/; HttpOnly"}
{"case":"over-cap","drained":65536,"cancelled":true,"cookie":"urbauth-~zod=xyz; Path=/; HttpOnly","note":"Stream cancelled after 64 KiB cumulative drain; cookie still available"}
{"case":"body-less-fallback","drained":-1,"cookie":"urbauth-~zod=fallback; Path=/; HttpOnly"}
```

- **Under-cap (1 KiB)**: drains fully, stream completes normally, cookie extracted.
- **Over-cap (256 KiB)**: drains exactly 65536 bytes (64 KiB), stream cancelled, cookie STILL extracted — the drain threshold prevents unbounded buffering without breaking auth.
- **Body-less fallback**: uses `text()` path, cookie extracted.

The 64 KiB threshold is intentionally a **cumulative read budget**, not a strict per-chunk allocation. Since `reader.read()` returns producer-defined chunks, a single chunk may push the total slightly above 64 KiB. This is safe: the threshold prevents unbounded accumulation, and the previous chunk (at most 64 KiB) is released before the next read.
