target.title: fix(cli-runner): restore history for SQLite-backed CLI resumes
target.body:
Related: #98236

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users resuming CLI-backed sessions would lose prior OpenClaw history after transcripts became SQLite-backed. Normal CLI, gateway, and cron paths persist a `sqlite:` transcript marker, but the CLI history loader still treated that marker as a filesystem path and reported that no transcript existed.

The same symptom could recur after moving a supported state-directory backup to a different absolute path because persisted markers retain the old path even though the restored per-agent database is now authoritative at the new location.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI runner now recognizes SQLite transcript markers, validates their session and agent identity, and reads from the current canonical store through the storage-neutral session accessor. The same canonical session target is passed through context-engine bootstrap, post-turn, and maintenance rewrites, so stale marker metadata cannot redirect reads or writes after a state-directory relocation.

The accessor streams only the newest complete rows within the existing 5 MiB JSONL-compatible window, restores the session envelope when the tail is truncated, and preserves migration, branch-safety, active-leaf selection, and message-cap behavior. Transcript existence uses a `LIMIT 1` lookup instead of synchronously aggregating every row on each CLI turn.

For retry and fallback paths where the current user turn was already persisted, history readers exclude that exact idempotency key after active-branch selection. This keeps the current turn out of lifecycle history, context-engine pre-prompt snapshots, and reseed `<conversation_history>` while preserving the same message once in `<next_user_message>`.

The previous short-header-read proposal and regression were intentionally removed as part of this PR redirect; this PR is now scoped to SQLite-backed CLI history restoration.

This is distinct from #108851, which bounds gateway message pagination through a derived active-message projection; it does not repair the CLI runner's marker existence or raw-history path. This change adds no schema, migration, configuration, default, or external public API surface.

## User Impact

CLI resumes, lifecycle hooks, context-engine synchronization, and allowed reseed flows can again use the active OpenClaw history stored in SQLite, including after a supported state-directory relocation. Retry and fallback turns no longer replay the current user message as prior history. Oversized transcripts remain bounded to the newest safe 5 MiB tail instead of loading the complete transcript.

## Evidence

- Initial RED on the test-first commit: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29512957643), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29512957643/job/87670775318) — 27 passed, 2 failed; marker existence returned `false` and oversized SQLite history returned `[]`.
- Review-gap RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29520108279), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29520108279/job/87694811630) — 31 passed, 2 failed; the relocated marker was rejected and existence still invoked full transcript stats.
- Memory-bound RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29522181652), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29522181652/job/87701667581) — tail selection still requested `event_json`, so an over-budget row was materialized before the JavaScript byte check.
- Context-target RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29524447512), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29524447512/job/87709238990) — the runtime transcript target still resolved a relocated session to the stale marker path.
- Live baseline RED through the real `pnpm openclaw agent --local` entry point with an isolated test-only CLI backend: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29549165465), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29549165465/job/87787840045) — the second turn saw zero prior messages and the provider gate blocked execution.
- Maintenance-target RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29553169268), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29553169268/job/87799830946) — the rewrite scope still included `storePath`, and file-backed maintenance was incorrectly converted to a SQLite marker.
- Persisted retry-turn RED on test-first commit `e141bfb6a441c48884f0d3698cce480f6bf4894e`, using the repository runner on Node 24.15.0 — 3 focused files failed as expected (3 failed, 94 passed): the current text appeared twice in the reseed prompt, hook/context-engine reads lacked the exclusion key, and SQLite history still contained the current turn.
- Final GREEN on exact fix head `d7a04d16f19baf2172ba45c654b2636497cf95a4`, pinned to base `44b01a1e5ab69357e46b0ec945b080290ef13873`: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29557720712), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29557720712/job/87813405498) — 10 focused files and 274 tests passed, including persisted retry-turn deduplication and a real two-database SQLite relocation rewrite control.
- The same exact-head job passed targeted `oxfmt`/`oxlint`, dependency-export deadcode checks, core `tsgo`, and patch whitespace validation.
- The same exact-head live proof ran two turns through `pnpm openclaw agent --local`: `sqlite_marker=true`, `second_hook_history_count=2`, both first-turn messages were present, the test-only CLI provider was invoked twice, and the second turn returned `provider-called`.
- Final `codex review --base origin/main` found no confirmed new defect; its Node 24.15.0 verification also passed 7 files / 168 tests and 3 adjacent files / 146 tests.

Verification covers the OpenClaw SQLite transcript-to-CLI-history production path on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 with Node 24, isolated state/config/workspace data, and a test-only CLI backend. It does not exercise a real third-party provider, browser, or cross-platform runtime.

target.title: fix(ai): bound openai-chatgpt-responses WebSocket with handshakeTimeout and maxPayload
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The `connectWebSocket` function in `openai-chatgpt-responses` creates a WebSocket connection without any handshake timeout or message size limit. If the server accepts TCP but never completes the WebSocket upgrade, the connection hangs indefinitely. Oversized messages could also cause OOM.

**Solution**: Implement transport-neutral bounds using the existing lifecycle cleanup path rather than `ws`-specific constructor options:
- **Handshake timeout**: `setTimeout`-based 30s deadline that calls `socket.close()` and rejects the promise. Unlike `ws`-specific `handshakeTimeout`, this works across Node, Bun, and browser globals.
- **Message size limit**: Per-frame byte check in `parseWebSocket` rejecting oversized messages with WebSocket close code 1009. Unlike `ws`-specific `maxPayload`, this is enforced at the message decoding layer regardless of runtime.
- **Regression tests**: Stalled-handshake timeout and oversized-message rejection tests using `vi.useFakeTimers` and mock WebSockets.

**What changed**: Two files:
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` — Added `CONNECT_WS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` (30s), `MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES` (16MB), handshake timer in `connectWebSocket()`, message size check in `parseWebSocket()`, test exports.
- Test file — Handshake timeout and oversized message regression coverage.

**What did NOT change**: No API changes, no `ws`-specific options on the constructor, no changes to `getWebSocketConstructor()`, `acquireWebSocket()`, or the SSE fallback path. No `docs/.local/` artifacts.

Fixes #109566

---

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #109566
- **In scope**: Transport-neutral handshake timeout + message size limit + regression tests
- **Out of scope**: WS-specific constructor options, SSE fallback, browser WebSocket globals

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Unbounded WebSocket handshake wait and oversized message OOM risk in openai-chatgpt-responses provider

**Real environment tested**: Test-only (transport-neutral bounds verified via `vi.useFakeTimers` and mock WebSocket classes)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
git diff packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```diff
+const CONNECT_WS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
+const MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
+
+const handshakeTimer = setTimeout(() => {
+  if (settled) return;
+  settled = true;
+  cleanup();
+  socket.close(WEBSOCKET_MESSAGE_TOO_BIG_CLOSE_CODE, "handshake timeout");
+  reject(new Error("WebSocket connection handshake timed out"));
+}, connectTimeoutMs ?? CONNECT_WS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS);
+handshakeTimer.unref?.();
+
+// In cleanup():
+clearTimeout(handshakeTimer);
+
+// In parseWebSocket onMessage:
+if (text.length > MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES) {
+  socket.close(WEBSOCKET_MESSAGE_TOO_BIG_CLOSE_CODE, "message exceeds size limit");
+  failed = new CodexProtocolError(...);
+  done = true;
+  wake();
+  return;
+}
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Both bounds are transport-neutral, working across Node, Bun, and browser globals. Handshake timeout uses `setTimeout` + `clearTimeout` — a standard JS pattern. Message size is checked at decode time, not at the WebSocket constructor level.

**What was not tested**: No real OpenAI API call. No real stalled-handshake scenario against OpenAI infrastructure.

---

## Tests and validation

```bash
pnpm test -- packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts
```

Two new tests:
1. `"rejects a stalled WebSocket upgrade with a handshake timeout error"` — verifies `connectWebSocket` rejects after timeout when socket never opens/errors/closes
2. `"rejects oversized WebSocket messages exceeding MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES"` — verifies `parseWebSocket` error on 17MB message

---

## Risk checklist

- [x] Backwards compatible — no API changes
- [x] Transport-neutral — works on Node, Bun, browser globals
- [x] Follows `clearTimeout`/`setTimeout` pattern used elsewhere in codebase (xai/tts.ts, realtime-voice-bridge.ts)
- [x] merge-risk: low — ~50 lines net, focused scope, regression tests added

target.title: fix(browser): keep tab reachability retry delay abortable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cancelling a browser tab operation during the reachability retry delay would wait the full delay before responding to the cancellation.

`ensureBrowserRunning` used `new Promise(setTimeout)` for the 250ms retry delay between reachability probes. When the request `AbortSignal` fired during this delay, the function waited the entire `TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS` before calling `signal.throwIfAborted()`, adding unnecessary latency to cancellation-sensitive callers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry delay now uses `sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal)` which rejects immediately when the signal fires, so the caller is notified of the cancellation during the delay rather than after it.

Related prior art: #108561 (discord gateway READY retry abortSignal), #108408 (feishu retry abortSignal propagation).

## User Impact

Browser tab operations (close, focus, select) cancelled during the 250ms reachability retry window respond to user cancellation up to 250ms faster.

## Evidence

### Scope

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Head | `eac9fd9a2f5` |
| Files | `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.ts` (+4/−5) · `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts` (+1/−1) |
| Net | +5 / −6 across 2 files |

### Production change (behavior)

```ts
// Before
await new Promise((resolve) => { setTimeout(resolve, RETRY_DELAY_MS); });
signal?.throwIfAborted();

// After
await sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal);
```

### Real-timer timing proof

A standalone Node.js script (`scripts/proof-109536-abort-timing.mjs`) compares the two patterns with real `performance.now()` timers and a real `AbortController`. Each scenario is run 5 times with the abort signal firing 50ms into the 250ms retry delay:

```
--- BEFORE (old code) ---
  Run 1: 250.6 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 2: 250.8 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 3: 250.3 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 4: 251.0 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 5: 250.2 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)

--- AFTER (new code: sleepWithAbort) ---
  Run 1: 50.5 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 2: 50.6 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 3: 50.5 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 4: 51.0 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 5: 50.8 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
```

- **BEFORE**: consistently ~250ms — always waits the full retry delay before noticing the abort.
- **AFTER**: consistently ~50ms — rejects as soon as the abort signal fires, eliminating up to 200ms of unnecessary wait.

The same abort-propagation invariant is additionally covered by the fake-timer unit test at `tabs.test.ts:345`.

### Local gates (touched surface)

| Gate | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts` | **22 passed** / 1 file |

### Proof

The existing test "does not retry or mutate after cancellation during the retry delay" covers this scenario: it advances past the first reachability check, aborts the signal, then verifies no reachability retry occurred. With `sleepWithAbort`, the abort is detected immediately during the delay rather than after it expires, and the error message changes from `"cancelled"` (from `throwIfAborted`) to `"aborted"` (from `sleepWithAbort`).

Real-timer proof confirms the timing improvement holds with real wall-clock timers, not only with fake timers.

target.title: fix(music): stop hanging when generated asset downloads drip forever
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where music generation providers (e.g. fal) could hang forever when a CDN dripped the audio body slowly enough to reset per-chunk idle timers. `fetchWithTimeout` clears its abort after headers land, so the download budget no longer applied to the body.

Additionally:
1. Restores transient HTTP retry that was lost when the non-2xx validation was placed outside `executeProviderOperationWithRetry`.
2. Skips diagnostic body reads for retryable 5xx statuses so a dripping error body does not consume the shared wall-clock deadline before the retry attempt starts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three changes in `downloadGeneratedMusicAsset`:

1. **Wall-clock deadline**: One deadline spans headers + non-2xx error-detail + successful-body reads via `readResponseTextPrefix` → `readResponseWithLimit({ timeoutMs, onTimeout })`.

2. **Retry inside the wrapper**: Bounded non-2xx status validation now runs inside `executeProviderOperationWithRetry`'s operation callback. When the CDN returns HTTP 503, the error is thrown inside the retry loop so `isTransientProviderOperationError` can retry it.

3. **Skip body reads for 5xx**: Retryable statuses (500/502/503/504) cancel the response body immediately instead of reading it for diagnostics. A dripping 5xx body could otherwise consume the full wall-clock deadline, leaving the retry attempt with effectively no remaining budget.

Non-overlapping: #108982 bounds video-generation downloads; #109076 bounds Discord webhook bodies.

## User Impact

- Generated music downloads fail within the configured timeout when a CDN body trickles forever.
- Transient CDN errors (503, etc.) with dripping bodies are retried immediately — the body is cancelled so the retry gets a full budget.
- Non-retryable errors (400, etc.) still include bounded diagnostic detail.
- Music generation no longer sticks forever on a slow-drip CDN response.

## Evidence

Exact head: `dee8f741c1da3899930e3602cf858d0e6072632d`

`oxfmt --check src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ bounds a dripping download body with one wall-clock deadline 284ms
 ✓ throws on non-2xx HTTP status without retry 18ms
 ✓ retries on transient HTTP status before succeeding 268ms
 ✓ skips diagnostic body read on retryable status so deadline survives for retry 264ms
 ✓ does not bound a dripping body when only chunk idle timeout is used 410ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

- **Drip body (200)**: continuous drip with timeoutMs=250 → rejects with wall-clock timeout.
- **Non-2xx (400)**: immediate 400 → throws HTTP status error without retry (400 is explicitly non-retryable), includes diagnostic body detail.
- **Retry (immediate 503 → 200)**: first request returns 503 with immediate body → retried → second request succeeds. Proves `requestCount === 2`.
- **Retry (dripping 503 → 200)**: first request returns 503 with continuous 15ms drip → body cancelled immediately (not read) → retry completes within 264ms. Proves the deadline survives for the retry attempt when the error body is skipped.
- **Negative control**: idle-only chunkTimeoutMs on a drip → stays unsettled past 400ms. Proves old code path has no wall-clock bound.

### Mutation check

Without fix (stash provider-assets.ts): `retries on transient` FAIL — 503 not retried.
With fix restored: `retries on transient` PASS — `requestCount === 2`.

### Not tested

Live fal CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(feishu): lock timeoutMs preflight abort for stalled DNS lookup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu app registration goes through `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. Operators need a locked regression that a **stalled DNS/proxy preflight** is cancelled by the guards existing top-level `timeoutMs` before any HTTP request is dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper P1 on the prior tip: replacing `timeoutMs` with `AbortSignal.timeout()` does **not** add preflight protection — `fetchWithSsrFGuard` already converts `timeoutMs` into the preflight abort signal via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, and swapping owners only drops the shared `request timed out` diagnostic.

**This iteration (rebased on latest main):**
- Rebuilt on latest `main` (`22563878857`)
- **Kept** guard `timeoutMs` (no production ownership change)
- Added stalled-lookup regression next to the existing hang-POST timeout proof, matching its outcome shape
- The registration API (`FeishuAppRegistrationFetchOptions`) is unchanged on current main — test typechecks and passes as-is
- Existing SSRF guard tests already cover stalled-DNS timeout at the guard level (`fetch-guard.ssrf.test.ts:1916,1939`); this Feishu test validates the full `beginAppRegistration` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call chain

## User Impact

- **Before:** No focused Feishu registration test that a never-resolving lookup aborts under `timeoutMs` without HTTP dispatch.
- **After:** That contract is locked; registration timeout semantics stay on the shared guard owner.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `6d7aab253ee`
**Base:** `22563878857`

### Before / After comparison

| Dimension | Before (no stalled-DNS test) | After (this PR adds regression) |
|---|---|---|
| DNS lookup stall coverage | ❌ Not tested | ✅ `stalledLookup` (never-resolving Promise) → aborted by `timeoutMs` |
| HTTP dispatch during preflight | ❌ Not verified | ✅ `fetchSpy not.toHaveBeenCalled()` — locked |
| Error type on stall | ❌ Not verified | ✅ Must be `TimeoutError` |
| Error message on stall | ❌ Not verified | ✅ Must be `"request timed out"` — shared diagnostic preserved |
| Stall timeout window | ❌ Not verified | ✅ `elapsedMs ≥ 60 && < 2000` — quick abort, no hang |
| Existing POST timeout test | ✅ Covers TCP-accept-no-headers path | ✅ Unchanged, same outcome shape |

### Matched outcome shape (new test vs existing POST sibling)

| Assertion | Existing POST hang test | New stalled-DNS test |
|---|---|---|
| `lookupFn` | real DNS lookup → `127.0.0.1` | `stalledLookup` (never resolves) |
| abort mechanism | `timeoutMs` → preflight AbortSignal | `timeoutMs` → preflight AbortSignal |
| outcome | `TimeoutError` / `request timed out` | `TimeoutError` / `request timed out` |
| `fetchImpl` | reaches TCP listener | ❌ **not called** (never reaches HTTP) |
| elapsed window | ≥60ms, <2000ms | ≥60ms, <2000ms |

### Full test suite (11/11 pass)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts --reporter verbose extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.10

 ✓ Feishu app registration > defaults unsafe begin polling lifetimes 183ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > clamps unsafe poll sleeps 13ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > prints scan-to-create QR codes 1ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > times out registration POSTs (TCP hang) 93ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > rejects with timeout when preflight lookup stalls 83ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > rejects Feishu API responses that exceed 16 MiB cap 178ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > parses under-cap JSON 19ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > sends bound reads through real SSRF guard 7ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > wraps malformed JSON with feishu.api error 6ms
 ✓ feishu bound reads > rejects oversized response (OOM guard) 82ms
 ✓ feishu bound reads > parses well-formed JSON under cap 14ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
   Start at  13:33:36
   Duration  2.72s

Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
Date: 2026-07-17T13:33:39+08:00
```

### Targeted stall test proof

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts --reporter verbose extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts -t "rejects with timeout when preflight lookup stalls"

[feishu preflight stall proof] timed_out=true name=TimeoutError elapsed_ms=81 fetch_called=0

```

**Output breakdown:**

| console.log field | Value | Assertion verified |
|---|---|---|
| `timed_out` | `true` | `expect(outcome.ok).toBe(false)` ✅ |
| `name` | `TimeoutError` | `expect(outcome.error.name).toBe("TimeoutError")` ✅ |
| `elapsed_ms` | `81` | `≥ 60 && < 2000` ✅ |
| `fetch_called` | `0` | `expect(fetchSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` ✅ |

target.title: fix(media): preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs in live test helpers truncation
target.body:
"## Summary

Replace `.slice()` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` in `redactLiveApiKey` to prevent cutting emoji or other supplementary-plane characters in half when redacting API keys in diagnostic output.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `redactLiveApiKey` used `String.prototype.slice()` at code-unit index boundaries (`.slice(0, 8)` and `.slice(-4)`), which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs producing orphaned surrogates in diagnostic output.

**Root Cause**: The function in `src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.ts:24` uses raw `.slice()` for display truncation without accounting for UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 8)` and `.slice(-4)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed.slice(-4), 4)`, which adjust the boundary away from surrogate pair splits.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.test.ts
```


target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix QA tool-progress timeout diagnostics shorten observed event bodies to a 240-code-unit preview. When an emoji began at the existing raw `slice(0, 237)` boundary, the later JSON diagnostic serialized only its high surrogate as an escaped `\ud83d`, discarding the complete character and making the timeout evidence misleading.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper now backs off to a complete Unicode code-point boundary while retaining the existing preview budget and suffix. Both preview-wait and final-wait diagnostics use the same formatter.

## User Impact

Matrix QA timeout failures no longer expose a half-character escape when observed messages cross the Unicode truncation boundary, so the retained failure evidence stays well-formed and actionable.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/matrix/scenarios/scenario-runtime-tool-progress-diagnostics.test.ts` (2 tests passed on Node 24.15.0)

target.title: fix(openai): prevent device-code login hangs on stalled requests
target.body:
Related: #104477

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running OpenAI device-code login could remain stuck indefinitely when an `auth.openai.com` request stopped responding before headers arrived or while its response body was being read.

The existing 15-minute authorization deadline only bounded the polling loop. A single user-code, poll, or token-exchange request could outlive that deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

All three device-code operations now use the canonical guarded OAuth HTTP lifecycle with a 30-second per-operation deadline, caller cancellation, HTTPS enforcement, audit context, bounded response reads, and deterministic resource release. Poll request deadlines are clamped to the remaining 15-minute authorization window; only timed-out polls retry, while caller cancellation still wins immediately.

When `HTTP_PROXY` or `HTTPS_PROXY` applies to an OpenAI auth URL, the request selects the same trusted environment-proxy guarded mode used by Google OAuth. `NO_PROXY` matches retain strict guarded fetch. This preserves the previous ambient proxy behavior while keeping the new timeout and SSRF policy.

This supersedes the closed #104477 implementation and incorporates its latest review request to use `fetchWithSsrFGuard` rather than a parallel raw-fetch timeout path. The 30-second policy aligns with the sibling OpenAI browser OAuth request boundary; it is not presented as an upstream Codex requirement.

## User Impact

OpenAI device-code login now fails clearly when the initial or final auth operation stalls, and transient stalled authorization polls can retry within the existing overall deadline. Ctrl-C and other caller cancellation behavior remains unchanged. Proxy-only environments continue to route device-code auth through their configured HTTP/S proxy.

No configuration, public API, endpoint, or happy-path authentication behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Exact head `02d608aa4e7d99970f072fbc46091d9654e7ca8c`, rebased onto `5f56a541d3df27f1e0dd67fab60cf43ab92d2c94`: Node 24.18.0 focused suite `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts` passed 15/15.
- Controlled production-path transport proof used `loginOpenAICodexDeviceCode` with its default fetch, a local CONNECT proxy, and a locally trusted `auth.openai.com` test certificate. The proxy observed `CONNECT auth.openai.com:443` and `POST /api/accounts/deviceauth/usercode` in both cases.
- Exact-head response-header stall: the TLS connection and POST completed, no response headers were sent, and the production path returned `OpenAI device code user code request timed out after 30000ms` after 30,070 ms; request sockets closed on abort.
- Exact-head response-body stall: the server sent `200 OK`, a declared 128-byte JSON body, and only the first byte; the same production timeout returned after 30,010 ms and request sockets closed on abort.
- Proxy regression coverage asserts `trusted_env_proxy` plus an actual `EnvHttpProxyAgent` dispatcher when HTTPS proxying applies, and asserts no mode override when `NO_PROXY` matches `auth.openai.com`.
- Live endpoint reachability through the patched production function: a real guarded user-code request reached `onVerification`, then a caller signal immediately stopped the flow. Redacted output: `{"verified":true,"cancelledAfterVerification":true}`. No user code, device id, or credentials were emitted.
- Happy-path coverage verifies that user-code, poll, and exchange requests all carry an `AbortSignal`.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed. Exact-head repository CI is authoritative for the broader plugin-SDK/type lanes.
- Full open-PR file scan at submission time covered 1,400 PRs and 12,239 changed files, including REST pagination for every PR above 100 files; neither changed file was present in another open PR.
- Fresh independent Codex adversarial review of the exact head found no actionable issue after checking the proxy compatibility repair, SSRF/timeout/body lifecycle, callers, sibling OpenAI OAuth path, tests, and sibling Codex source.
- Direct Codex source inspection confirms the same device-code endpoints and 15-minute overall polling window ([device flow](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/5c19155cbd93bfa099016e7487259f61669823ff/codex-rs/login/src/device_code_auth.rs#L62-L108)); its HTTP client exposes a per-request timeout API but does not prescribe 30 seconds ([client API](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/5c19155cbd93bfa099016e7487259f61669823ff/codex-rs/http-client/src/default_client.rs#L129-L131)).

target.title: fix(video-generation): DashScope downloads hang when CDN body stalls after headers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two issues with DashScope-compatible video downloads:

1. **Stalled CDN body hang**: After headers returned, no chunk-idle timeout was wired into `readResponseWithLimit`, so a stalled body could wait the full request budget instead of failing with a clear idle timeout.
2. **Exhausted deadline initiates network I/O**: A function-valued remaining deadline that returned 0 (budget consumed by header fetch) was checked AFTER `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` had already sent bytes over the wire. The guard now runs before fetch.

Affected workflow: `runDashscopeVideoGenerationTask` → `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` → `readResponseWithLimit`.

## Why This Change Was Made

At `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos`, the resolved `downloadTimeoutMs` is now:
- **Checked before fetch**: a non-positive remaining budget throws immediately without network I/O, matching the sibling Google video download path's behavior.
- **Passed as `chunkTimeoutMs`** + `onIdleTimeout` into `readResponseWithLimit`, so stalled bodies fail with `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` instead of a generic `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` deadline.

`fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` already keeps its abort until `release()`, so a continuously dripping CDN body cannot hang forever; the chunk-idle bound is the download-owned stall signal that was missing.

Non-goals: changing shared `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded`, `readResponseWithLimit`, or `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`.

Collision check: no open PR on `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` / `src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts`.

## User Impact

- Stalled DashScope video downloads fail with `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` instead of a generic request timeout or full-budget wait.
- Already-exhausted remaining budgets fail immediately without network I/O.
- Continuously dripping bodies still die within the existing guarded request deadline.

## Evidence

Exact head: `920b47be7e9a11c1fbb78845226d51aca97afdf8`

`oxfmt --check src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ aborts a stalled generated video body via chunk idle timeout 511ms
 ✓ persists a complete generated video body before the idle deadline 5ms
 ✓ fails closed before fetch when a function-valued remaining budget is exhausted 5ms
 ✓ bounds a stalled loopback HTTP body with a real server 220ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Key contract changes

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Exhausted deadline checked after `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` (network I/O already initiated) | Checked before fetch — throws immediately, `fetchFn` not called |
| Body had no chunk-idle timeout → stalled bodies hit generic request timeout | `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` wired → `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` |

### Loopback proof

Real `http.createServer` returns HTTP 200 + one chunk then stalls. Real `fetch` + real `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` with `timeoutMs: 200` rejects within 5s (~220ms observed) — bounded, not an indefinite hang.

### Not tested

Live DashScope CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(gateway): bound config file opener
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening the configured file from the Control UI could wait indefinitely when a platform opener did not exit. A single hard timeout is not safe on Linux because `xdg-open` may synchronously own a successfully opened foreground editor.

## Why This Change Was Made

The opener lifecycle now follows each platform contract:

- macOS `open` and Windows `Start-Process` retain a five-second launcher deadline;
- Linux `xdg-open` runs detached with ignored stdio and `unref()`, while the gateway observes only the first five seconds for immediate launcher failures;
- a long-lived Linux foreground handler is treated as launched and is never killed.

The configuration-specific lifecycle is isolated in `config-open.ts`; the shared `open-path.ts` contract used by session workspace reveal remains unchanged.

## User Impact

The `config.openFile` RPC no longer waits forever. Linux users can keep foreground editors opened by `xdg-open`, while missing-command and headless failures retain the existing actionable response. macOS and Windows launcher waits remain bounded.

## Evidence

- Exact rebased head: `55f04309cea509a0cae81fe1cdbc88f53ff53643` on current `origin/main` `96815a437b33872ee55c70c4fb10eb7e5c942506`.
- Node 24.18.0 focused suite: `src/gateway/server-methods/config-open.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts`, 36/36 tests passed.
- Focused tests cover platform command selection, five-second launcher timeout options, immediate Linux failures, long-lived detached Linux handlers, error normalization, and headless classification.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed on all four changed files.
- Controlled Linux proof on the unchanged rebased implementation: a long-lived `xdg-open`-style child returned after the five-second observation window without `kill`, while a real no-handler probe returned exit code 3 and was classified as headless.
- Independent Codex adversarial review of the final lifecycle found no actionable runtime bug; Execa 9.6.1 detached/reject/cleanup semantics and the gateway RPC caller were checked directly.

Proof gap: native macOS and Windows opener scenarios were not available in this Linux environment; their paths are covered by the focused launcher contract tests and retain the existing `runExec` timeout behavior.

AI-assisted: yes. No generated code was accepted without focused tests and independent review.

target.title: Create Claw-managed workspace files
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the third [RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27) slice, stacked on [#101755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755):

- Creates canonical bootstrap files and supporting `workspace.files` only inside the new Claw agent workspace.
- Uses OpenClaw fs-safe roots with traversal, symlink, hardlink, nonregular-file, and size rejection.
- Revalidates source content against the consented plan digest immediately before each write.
- Uses create-only writes and never overwrites pre-existing content.
- Persists a pending per-file owner row before each write, then records complete or failed status with canonical package-relative source and workspace-relative destination paths.
- Defines the workspace ledger in OpenClaw's shared generated SQLite schema instead of creating an ad hoc runtime table.
- Retains written-file evidence and marks the root install partial if a later file or provenance update fails.
- Propagates the consented `planIntegrity` through complete and partial add results.

Package, MCP, and cron mutation remain blocked until their canonical owner slices. No declared component is silently skipped.

## Stack

- RFC: [openclaw/rfcs#27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27)
- Depends on: [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) schema/source identity/read-only plan
- Depends on: [#101755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755) consented agent/workspace creation and root provenance
- This PR: confined workspace files, hashes, and per-file ownership
- Next: [#102228](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102228) skill/plugin package owners

## Validation

```text
pnpm exec vitest run src/claws/workspace.test.ts src/claws/provenance.test.ts \
  src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts
# passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts \
  src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts
# lifecycle E2E passed

pnpm exec oxlint src/claws/add.ts src/claws/workspace.ts \
  src/claws/workspace.test.ts src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts
# 0 warnings, 0 errors

pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm tsgo:test:src
git diff --check
# passed
```

The real CLI E2E previews the workspace Claw, applies the exact emitted plan in the same isolated state directory, and verifies `SOUL.md`, `HEARTBEAT.md`, and `reference/policy.md` plus their complete SQLite owner rows.

Codex review of the final uncommitted patch completed with no actionable findings.

This PR adds stable dev/mock-only fixture sessions to the Control UI mock server. The proposed fixtures cover a New session empty state, a coding session, a response-shape showcase, and a markdown showcase without changing production gateway or session APIs.

target.title: feat(cli): improve editor handoffs for agents and humans
target.body:
## Summary

- add `crabbox open --json` with a versioned `crabbox/editor-handoff/v1` object for agents and other automation
- keep stdout machine-readable while workspace notices and diagnostics remain on stderr
- make the default terminal output easier to scan and copy with labeled SSH-command and remote-folder blocks
- state the foreground lease-activity, hard-TTL, Ctrl-C, and release behavior directly in the handoff
- document the child-process pattern for agents consuming the JSON handshake

## Why

https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/1127 establishes the right generalized `open --editor=<name>` abstraction, but its only output is human prose and the command intentionally remains running. That makes agents scrape text and guess how to manage the foreground keepalive process, while humans have to select command and path values embedded inside numbered sentences.

This follow-up preserves the safety model from that PR: no background daemon, no SSH config or editor-setting mutation, no credential persistence, and no editor auto-launch.

## Agent UX

`--json` emits one newline-terminated object before waiting:

- editor identity
- lease id
- complete shell-quoted SSH command
- exact remote folder
- GitHub Actions hydration state
- foreground lease-activity and hard-TTL semantics
- release command when available

An agent can spawn Crabbox, decode the first object, use the handoff, and retain the child-process handle for the editor session.

## Human UX

The default output now provides:

- a clear ready state
- dedicated `SSH command` and `Remote folder` blocks
- short next steps
- explicit foreground activity and hard-TTL guidance
- a visible release command

## Validation

- `gofmt -w internal/cli/open.go internal/cli/open_test.go`
- added focused coverage for the human output and JSON contract
- full repository checks left to GitHub Actions because this execution environment could not clone GitHub or run the complete checkout

## Security and configuration

No secrets, configuration files, SSH config, or editor settings are written. Existing target restrictions and shell quoting are preserved.

target.title: refactor(gateway-client): expose request dispatch boundary
target.body:
Related: #96230

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway-internal callers can observe a request result or a later `accepted` response, but cannot distinguish a failure before the request frame entered the local WebSocket transport from a failure after dispatch. That distinction is required before later restart-recovery work can make conservative retry or refund decisions without guessing from promise settlement.

This is the first independently reviewable dependency extracted from #96230. The original PR remains frozen while its behavior is split into ordered, narrower changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The protocol client is the only layer that owns the synchronous `socket.send(...)` boundary, so this adds an optional `onDispatched` observer immediately after `send` returns successfully and routes it through the existing callback-isolation helper. The package client and high-level `callGateway` wrapper forward the same observer without changing request frames, protocol versions, timeout/abort cleanup, reconnect behavior, or `onAccepted` response semantics.

The observer contract is intentionally narrow: it means the request frame was handed to the local WebSocket transport. It does not mean the Gateway/server accepted or processed the request. The request option type lives in a dedicated small module and is re-exported from the existing protocol-client module, preserving import and structural type compatibility. `GatewayClient` forwards that shared option shape as a unit, then overrides only its normalized `expectFinal` and `timeoutMs` values; this keeps the oversized implementation LOC-neutral without deleting unrelated comments.

This is a root-cause boundary fix: higher layers no longer need to infer whether transport dispatch happened. The gateway-client package is private and the new field is additive and optional. A consumer/test-double sweep covered the package export, OpenClaw facade, SDK transport, accepted-response caller, both affected request stubs, and the node-host bridge. The node-host bridge only forwards `timeoutMs` across its IPC boundary, so later recovery code must use `callGateway` or introduce a separate IPC dispatch acknowledgement rather than assuming this observer is available there.

Out of scope for this PR: Plugin SDK/session-state isolation, recovery persistence, `mainRestartRecovery` admission or ownership, bounded recovery, quarantine, and Doctor repair. In particular, this PR does not write any production recovery state.

## User Impact

There is no direct end-user behavior change. Existing callers behave exactly as before; later recovery PRs can use a precise local transport-dispatch fact instead of broad failure inference.

Risk is limited to an additive observer callback. It is not invoked when WebSocket send throws, observer exceptions are isolated from request settlement, and the callback must not be interpreted as server acceptance.

## Evidence

Focused TDD reproduction before the original implementation:

```text
expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times
```

Exact CI repair reproduction on failed head `166b22c`, against event base `6d31c16`:

```text
1231  1230  grew  packages/gateway-client/src/client.ts
TypeScript LOC ratchet failed: oversized legacy files may not grow.
```

The repaired committed tree passes the same exact-base ratchet and leaves the file at 1229 lines versus 1230 on the base. Complete affected test files also pass:

```text
TypeScript LOC ratchet: checked 4 changed production files.
Gateway client watchdog: 19 passed (19)
Gateway call wrapper:     119 passed (119)
```

Real behavior proof used an isolated OpenClaw Gateway and the production `callGateway -> GatewayClient -> GatewayProtocolClient` path for an authenticated `health` RPC over a real loopback WebSocket:

```text
onDispatched calls: 1
Callback ran before response resolution: true
Callback intentionally threw: yes
Request still resolved successfully: yes
```

The send-exception regression also verifies that `onDispatched` is not called when `socket.send` fails and that pending request state is cleaned up.

Repository and package gates:

```text
Gateway-client package build: passed, including generated declarations
Scoped lint: passed
Scoped formatting: passed for all 6 changed files
```

On the failed head, hosted `check-prod-types` and `check-test-types` both passed; the only primary code failure was the LOC ratchet, with `openclaw/ci-gate` failing as its aggregate. Updated hosted CI will rerun those lanes on the repaired head.

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text
initializer 2: failed (1)
initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1
```

Final head:

```text
initializer 5: ok
initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

The final table is usable, all six initializers return successfully, and the temporary schema row is removed.

### Tests and gates

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 2 files and 126 tests passed.
- `check:changed` passed conflict markers, the TypeScript LOC ratchet, attributions, extension export guards, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and formatting. Its repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline reports a hash mismatch; the exact baseline command reproduces the same mismatch on a clean detached `origin/main` snapshot, so this PR does not introduce it.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Earlier exact-head failures were deterministic regressions on the old `main` baseline and did not reference either memory-lancedb file. The current `main` repair at [`2c95bd2387c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2c95bd2387cdcfab5b3736f3ab6d08a4ad23cb65) is included; fresh exact-head CI run [29386264145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29386264145) passed with 46 checks green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.

Remote Testbox delegation was unavailable because the installed Crabbox binary is 0.16.0 while the current flow requires 0.22.0 or newer. The proof above is secretless local execution, and GitHub CI remains the remote verification lane.

target.title: feat(cua): add experimental read-only diagnostics provider
target.body:
## Summary

Adds an experimental CUA provider for read-only diagnostics and existing-sandbox inventory.

The provider is intentionally registered as service control, not delegated execution. It supports:

- `crabbox doctor --provider cua`
- `crabbox list --provider cua`
- `crabbox status --provider cua --id <existing-sandbox-id>`
- trusted local configuration, environment-only credentials, provider metadata, documentation, and a non-mutating smoke test

All remote lifecycle mutation fails closed before the CUA SDK can perform it. Create, warmup, run, stop, cleanup, and bridge deletion are disabled.

## Safety gate

The pinned upstream create API has no idempotency key or client-assigned identity echoed by create, list, and get. A create that succeeds server-side but times out client-side can therefore leave a billed sandbox that Crabbox cannot identify safely.

Deletion is also disabled because the current API cannot atomically bind deletion to an immutable sandbox identity; verify-then-delete by mutable name has a replacement race.

Tracking: https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/381

## Verification

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: feat(fal): add SSH lease provider
target.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/694

## Summary

Adds a direct fal Compute SSH lease provider with Crabbox-managed SSH and sync support, local-claim-owned cleanup, and the `fal-ai` alias.

This also adds fal provider docs, provider matrix metadata, benchmark category generation, and an opt-in guarded live smoke script that defaults to no live provider mutation unless `CRABBOX_LIVE=1` and fal is selected.

## Lifecycle safety

- Uses the fal Compute `Idempotency-Key` header with the Crabbox lease ID for creates.
- Fsyncs the SSH keypair, exact create-request binding, and pre-mutation intent before any paid provider call; an untouched intent can be cancelled without creating a resource.
- Durably syncs every guarded claim publication and removal, including newly created state-directory ancestors, before treating ownership transitions as complete.
- Holds a cross-process acquisition-lifetime lock through ready publication and marks participating claims durably; cleanup retains unmarked legacy transitional claims rather than mistaking an older live acquisition for an abandoned one.
- Publishes a unique in-flight claim revision for every same-key POST and atomically records a known ID, retains an indeterminate outcome, or removes a first-attempt rejection.
- Bounds ambiguous-create replay to fal's documented idempotency window and treats rate limits as explicit rejections.
- Applies that bound as an actual request deadline in both immediate and stop-time replay, preserving a safety margin before provider idempotency expiry.
- Persists a cleanup-only provisional claim immediately after a provider ID is known, before readiness or SSH setup.
- Binds claims to the canonical API endpoint and a one-way credential fingerprint; lifecycle calls fail closed after endpoint or account changes.
- Serializes destructive actions under compare-and-swap claim locks, including mixed-credential cleanup.
- Serializes same-lease mutations and fal slug allocation across processes, including final ready publication and rollback claim recovery.
- Serializes ambiguous-create recovery, winner adoption, and persistence-failure cleanup so concurrent stops cannot delete the winning instance or orphan a known billable instance.
- If a provisional claim disappears mid-acquire, proves account-wide absence or reclaims/deletes the exact in-memory instance under an expected-absent claim lock; ambiguous cleanup recreates the known-ID recovery claim.
- Reconciles ambiguous unclaimed creates against complete paginated provider inventory without deleting resources Crabbox cannot prove it owns.
- Requires the documented complete fal inventory envelope before accepting a zero-resource proof, and polls raw provider inventory back to the pre-create fingerprint after stop.
- Rolls back callback/readiness/bootstrap failures unless `--keep` explicitly owns a failed-acquire recovery claim.
- Cleanup removes provider-absent local claims before TTL filtering and only deletes local-claim-owned fal instances.
- Persists delete-attempt and delete-accepted states, never replays an accepted DELETE, and requires exact `GET 404` plus complete inventory omission plus a second exact `GET 404` before removing the key and claim.
- Rejects cross-origin bearer redirects, method-rewriting mutation redirects, escaped API base paths, unsafe SSH login names, and unbounded provider requests before any credential-bearing mutation or SSH invocation.

target.title: feat(providers): add local Lume macOS leases
target.body:
## Summary

- add a native `lume` SSH-lease provider for local Apple-silicon macOS VMs
- clone one stopped golden image into one isolated VM per Crabbox lease
- rotate SSH host keys on first clone boot, pin a per-lease host identity, and inject only a unique public key
- serialize acquisition and enforce Apple's two-running-macOS-guest host limit
- identity-fence the detached `lume run` owner, work around Lume 0.3.16 stop/readiness defects, and verify stop/delete before claim cleanup
- add claim-safe release and multi-storage cleanup, trusted configuration, ARM64 target validation, docs, metadata, and live-smoke dispatch
- add reusable macOS image hooks for first-boot identity and optional Cua Driver startup, plus noninteractive developer-tool setup improvements

## Why

Crabbox needs a local macOS backend that can reuse layered Lume images without baking credentials into them. Each session should have its own VM, filesystem, machine identity, SSH key, and host-key trust while still supporting normal Crabbox sync/run/release behavior.

This is separate from #678, which adds a cloud Linux CUA provider; this PR covers local macOS VMs on user-owned Apple-silicon infrastructure.

## Validation

- `go test -race ./internal/providers/lume ./internal/providers/all -count=1`
- `go vet ./internal/providers/lume ./internal/providers/all`
- full `go test ./internal/cli -count=1`
- Windows ARM64 cross-compilation of the Lume provider
- docs, provider-matrix, shell syntax, plist, and Node live-smoke checks
- real Apple-silicon lifecycle with two concurrent leases from the same stopped golden image:
  - distinct VM names, IPs, platform UUIDs, SSH keypairs, and ED25519 host-key fingerprints
  - independent Crabbox commands at the same guest path
  - Cua Accessibility, Screen Recording, and actual desktop capture passed in both VMs
  - Tailscale remained installed but logged out with `NeedsLogin` in both VMs
  - concurrent release left no VM, owner process, claim, key, known-hosts, private log, or temporary password-helper residue

## Current boundaries

- macOS/ARM64 only; Lume is not used for Windows or Linux guests
- the prepared guest currently needs Lume's default bootstrap account/password; custom bootstrap passwords are not yet supported
- desktop/webVNC bridging and Crabbox-managed Tailscale enrollment are intentionally not advertised yet
- reusable image layers remain credential-free; credentials are injected only into disposable clones after boot

target.title: feat: validate required run artifacts against a schema (`--require-artifact-schema`)
target.body:
Closes #1070 

---

## Summary

Adds a post-run evidence gate that validates a required artifact's **JSON content** against a declared schema, not just its existence. Today `--require-artifact` is — per `docs/features/artifacts.md` — *"an existence guard, not manifest validation"*, so a run passes its proof gate even when the proof file is empty, truncated, or missing the fields that make it evidence. `--require-artifact-schema remote=schema.json` closes that gap: present → **valid**.

```sh
crabbox run \
  --require-artifact-schema docs/metrics/hermetic-agents-e2e.json=schemas/hermetic.schema.json \
  -- ./scripts/run_hermetic_agents_demo.sh
```

Missing, unparseable, or non-conforming → `exit 7` with the exact violations listed. Malformed schema file → `exit 2` at preflight.

## Motivation

Directly addresses the gap named in `docs/features/hermetic-agent-evidence.md`: *"Crabbox can require that the proof file exists; it does not validate the proof schema."* Strengthens the hermetic-agent, test-result, and manifest evidence flows for a tool whose contract is reproducible, reviewable run evidence.

## What changed

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `internal/cli/run_artifact_schema.go` | **New.** Dependency-free JSON-Schema-subset validator, the `remote=schema.json` spec parser + preflight loader, and the SSH fetch/validate gate helper. |
| `internal/cli/run_artifact_schema_test.go` | **New.** Table-driven unit tests for the validator, spec parser, and loader. |
| `internal/cli/run.go` | Flag registration, preflight load, `--sync-only` rejection, delegated-provider guard, the post-run gate hook, and evidence attachment. |
| `internal/cli/timing.go` | New `TimingReport.SchemaValidations` field (`omitempty`). |
| `docs/features/artifacts.md` | Documents the new flag next to the existence-guard note. |

Net: most of the change is the new validator (~380 lines) and its tests
(~335 lines, including fail-closed, byte-cap, and injected-reader gate coverage);
the wiring in `run.go` is +26 lines.

## Design decisions

- **Zero new dependency, fail-closed.** The schema language is a small subset of
  JSON Schema (`type`, `required`, `properties`, `items`, `enum`). Parsing is
  **fail-closed** via `json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields`: any unsupported
  validation keyword (`pattern`, `minimum`, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf`,
  `$ref`, …) is rejected at preflight with `exit 2`, at every nesting level, so a
  passing gate always means the supplied constraints were actually enforced.
  Only annotation keywords (`$schema`, `$id`, `title`, `description`, `$comment`,
  `examples`, `default`, `deprecated`) are accepted and ignored. The subset can
  be widened deliberately later.
- **Validation is local, and bounded.** Artifact bytes are read into memory via
  the existing `runSSHOutput` base64 transport (never written to the working
  tree), and the read is **capped at 5 MiB** — the remote command reads one byte
  past the limit (`head -c` / a bounded PowerShell read) and the decoder rejects
  anything larger, so an oversized or runaway artifact fails the gate instead of
  flooding SSH output and exhausting local memory. Keeping validation in Go makes
  it provider-agnostic and unit-testable.
- **Mirrors the existing gate.** Runs after command success alongside
  `--require-artifact`, reuses its `exit 7` gate class and safe-path validation
  (`validateRequiredRunArtifactGlobs`), and follows the `stringListFlag` pattern.
- **Distinct error taxonomy.** Command failure keeps its own exit code; malformed
  schema → `exit 2` (preflight); missing/unfetchable or non-conforming artifact
  → `exit 7`.
- **SSH-backed first.** Delegated-run providers reject the flag at preflight
  (`exit 2`), mirroring how `--require-artifact` collection and other artifact
  features are already gated behind an explicit delegated capability. Delegated
  support is a follow-up.

## Evidence schema

```json
{
  "schemaValidations": [
    {
      "artifact": "docs/metrics/hermetic-agents-e2e.json",
      "schema": "schemas/hermetic.schema.json",
      "valid": false,
      "violations": [
        "qa_verdict: missing required property \"qa_verdict\"",
        "count: expected type number, got string"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`omitempty`, so timing JSON is byte-identical when the flag is unused.

## Testing / verification

The valuable core — `validateJSONAgainstSchema`, `parseArtifactSchema`, the spec parser, and the loader — is pure stdlib with no lease/network/provider dependency. It is covered by table-driven tests:

- valid document → no violations; missing required / wrong type / `enum` mismatch → violation at the right path;
- nested object and `items[i]` index paths reported correctly;
- non-JSON and empty documents → a single `json` violation, not a crash;
- type mismatch does not cascade into child violations;
- malformed schema → `exit 2` (distinct from `exit 7`);
- **fail-closed:** `pattern`, `minimum`, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf`, `$ref`, and a nested unsupported keyword are each rejected at preflight; annotation keywords are accepted;
- **bounded fetch:** `decodeBoundedBase64` rejects oversized payloads and the remote command carries the `head -c` byte bound;
- **gate behaviour (via an injected reader, no live SSH):** valid → pass, invalid content → `exit 7` with violations, fetch error → `exit 7`, oversized → `exit 7` — asserting results, ordering, and exit codes;
- spec parsing: valid `remote=schema.json`, missing `=`, unsafe/absolute/`..` remote path; missing, malformed, and duplicate specs → `exit 2`.

**Verified locally:** the validator, spec/loader, byte-cap, and gate logic were extracted verbatim into a standalone module and run with `go test` — all tests pass, `go vet` clean.

> **Note for CI:** this development environment cannot compile the full
> `internal/cli` package because the repo pins future-dated modules
> (`google.golang.org/api@v0.282.0`, `genproto@…20260526…`) that the public
> `proxy.golang.org` returns `403` for (they resolve only via the private
> proxy). The gate's ordering, exit codes, and evidence are now covered by
> injected-reader unit tests, so what remains unverified locally is specifically
> the live SSH transport and full-package integration — a redacted live
> transcript (valid / invalid / missing / oversized / malformed-schema) should be
> attached from CI or a real SSH-backed lease. Run:

```sh
gofmt -l $(git ls-files '*.go')
go vet ./...
go build -trimpath -o bin/crabbox ./cmd/crabbox
go test -race ./internal/cli/
```

## Non-goals / follow-ups

- Not a data-safety / secrets scanner (stays a separate concern).
- Not remote validation; not a JUnit/`results` replacement.
- Widening the supported keyword subset, making the 5 MiB cap configurable, and a delegated-provider capability contract are documented follow-ups.

## Addressing review (ClawSweeper / Codex, blocked → resolved)

- **[P2] Unbounded remote read → resource exhaustion.** Fixed. The fetch is now
  capped at 5 MiB: `remoteBoundedReadBase64Command` reads `maxBytes+1` bytes and
  `decodeBoundedBase64` rejects anything over the limit, with oversized-path unit
  tests. (`internal/cli/run_artifact_schema.go`)
- **[P2] Silently ignoring unsupported schema keywords → false proof.** Fixed by
  making parsing fail-closed (`DisallowUnknownFields`) and rejecting unsupported
  validation keywords at preflight, with tests for `pattern` / `minimum` /
  `additionalProperties` / `anyOf` / `$ref`. Docs no longer claim general JSON
  Schema compatibility. This adopts the reviewer's recommended
  **"fail closed on keywords"** contract.
- **Real behaviour proof.** Gate ordering, exit codes, and evidence are now
  exercised by injected-reader unit tests. A live SSH/CLI transcript still needs
  to come from CI or a real lease, because this environment cannot build the full
  `internal/cli` package (private future-dated modules; see the CI note above) —
  not because the gate logic is unverified.

Closes the schema-validation gap tracked in `docs/features/hermetic-agent-evidence.md`.
